title: Spectral Analysis Of Equilibration: Information Leakage In Isolated Quantum Systems
authors: Andr\'e T. Ces\'ario, Marcos G. Alpino, Reinaldo O. Vianna, Tiago Debarba
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified dynamical-spectral framework for equilibration in isolated quantum systems based on a subspace coarse-graining approach. Central to our formulation is the Leakage Fidelity Function (LFF), defined as the probability that a unitarily evolving state escapes the support of its initial subspace. This quantity provides a direct, operational measure of information flow and memory loss without invoking ensemble assumptions or perturbative arguments. We derive universal bounds on temporal fluctuations of the LFF, in terms of the spectral gap structure and the square of the effective dimension, evincing that large spectral delocalization suppresses fluctuations and guarantees equilibration on average. By introducing spectral power distributions and associated entropic measures, we establish a quantitative link between phase mixing, gap participation, and dynamical stability. We further investigate the equilibration timescale by connecting the LFF to quantum speed limits, thereby revealing the average time required for equilibration. Our results provide a state-dependent, geometrically transparent perspective on how spectral complexity and subspace information leakage jointly govern irreversibility in closed quantum many-body systems.
tldr: A unified dynamical-spectral framework for equilibration in isolated quantum systems using a subspace coarse-graining approach and a new measure called Leakage Fidelity Function.
motivation: To understand how information leaks and memory is lost in closed quantum systems without ensemble assumptions, and to connect spectral properties to equilibration dynamics.
method: Introduces the Leakage Fidelity Function (LFF) as an operational measure of information flow, derives universal bounds on its fluctuations using spectral gap structure and effective dimension, and links it to quantum speed limits.
result: Large spectral delocalization suppresses fluctuations and guarantees equilibration on average; the LFF provides a quantitative link between phase mixing, gap participation, and dynamical stability.
conclusion: The framework offers a state-dependent, geometrically transparent perspective on how spectral complexity and subspace information leakage govern irreversibility in closed quantum many-body systems.

title: New Bounds On Private Simultaneous Quantum Message Passing
authors: Uma Girish, Alex May, Natalie Parham, Henry Yuen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the private simultaneous message (PSM) setting, [MATH] players obtain inputs [MATH] and then each send messages to a referee, who should learn [MATH] but no other information about [MATH]. The PSM setting was introduced as a minimal model for secure multiparty computation and has connections to Boolean function complexity. In the quantum setting, PSM has been related to non-local quantum computation (NLQC). The communication and correlation cost of implementing PSM remains poorly understood. Here, we give new upper and lower bounds on the (quantum) PSM model. For lower bounds, we show: 1) Neiporuk's measure lower bounds the entanglement required for [MATH]-player quantum PSM with perfect correctness. This leads to quadratic lower bounds for explicit functions. 2) The rank of the communication matrix of [MATH] lower bounds 2-player quantum PSM with perfect privacy but imperfect correctness. This implies a previously unknown lower bound on classical PSM with imperfect correctness. When allowing quantum communication and shared entanglement, these are the first lower bounds on quantum PSM that make use of the privacy condition. For upper bounds, we show: 1) Letting [MATH] be the size of a quantum circuit computing [MATH], [MATH] be the circuit depth, [MATH] the number of players, [MATH] the number of bits received by each player, and [MATH] a correctness parameter, we obtain [MATH]. 2) The square of the Fourier 1 norm of [MATH], [MATH], upper bounds the classical PSM complexity, [MATH]. In proving the first upper bound, we generalize existing [MATH]-depth based techniques for NLQC from [MATH] to [MATH] parties, and consider cases where the Clifford layers are restricted to having small light cones.
tldr: This paper provides new lower and upper bounds on the communication and entanglement costs of private simultaneous quantum message passing, connecting to non-local quantum computation and Boolean function complexity.
motivation: The private simultaneous message (PSM) model is a minimal setting for secure multiparty computation, and its quantum version has ties to non-local quantum computation. The communication and correlation costs of quantum PSM are poorly understood, motivating new bounds.
method: The authors prove lower bounds using Neiporuk's measure and communication matrix rank, and upper bounds via quantum circuit size and depth, as well as Fourier 1-norm.
result: They obtain quadratic lower bounds for explicit functions, a lower bound on classical PSM with imperfect correctness, and upper bounds scaling with circuit size and depth, and with the square of the Fourier 1-norm.
conclusion: These results advance the understanding of quantum PSM complexity and its relation to NLQC, providing the first lower bounds that leverage the privacy condition in the quantum setting.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the private simultaneous message (PSM) model in both classical and quantum settings, focusing on communication and correlation costs. In the PSM model, k players each receive an n-bit input and send a single message to a referee, who must compute a function f of all inputs while learning nothing else. The quantum version (QPSM) allows quantum messages and shared entanglement. The authors provide new lower bounds: (1) Nečiporuk's measure lower bounds the entanglement required for k-player quantum PSM with perfect correctness, yielding quadratic lower bounds for explicit functions. (2) The rank of the communication matrix of a two-player function f lower bounds the quantum PSM cost with perfect privacy but imperfect correctness, implying a new classical lower bound. For upper bounds, they show: (1) For a function f computable by a quantum circuit of size s and depth d_f, the quantum PSM cost is at most (kn + s) * log^{O(d_f)}(s/ε), where ε is the error. (2) The classical PSM complexity is bounded by O(||f̂||_1^2), the square of the Fourier 1-norm. The first upper bound generalizes T-depth-based techniques for non-local quantum computation (NLQC) from 2 to k parties, considering restricted Clifford layers.

Quadratic lower bounds on entanglement for explicit functions in k-player quantum PSM with perfect correctness.

Upper bound on classical PSM complexity via Fourier 1-norm: PSM(f) ≤ O(||f̂||_1^2).

For lower bounds, it adapts Nečiporuk's measure—a combinatorial complexity measure—to the quantum PSM setting, showing that it lower bounds the required entanglement. This involves constructing a communication matrix and relating its rank to privacy constraints. The rank lower bound for imperfect correctness uses the fact that the referee's output distribution must be close to the correct function value, leading to a rank-based bound via linear algebra. For upper bounds, the authors design explicit protocols. The quantum upper bound uses a circuit decomposition into Clifford+T gates, leveraging T-depth to parallelize operations and reduce communication. They extend prior 2-party NLQC protocols to k parties by grouping players and using shared entanglement to simulate non-local gates. The classical upper bound uses Fourier analysis: they encode the function's Fourier coefficients into messages, achieving communication proportional to the squared 1-norm.

title: Measurement Geometry For Quantum Random Access Codes: Beyond Nayak Bound And Toward Optimality
authors: Seiseki Akibue, Rudy Raymond, Suguru Tamaki, Kosei Teramoto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum random access codes (QRACs) ask how well N classical bits can be encoded into M qubits while allowing any single bit to be recovered. Although the Nayak bound remains the standard general upper bound on the decoding probability, numerical evidence suggests a stronger upper bound in the small-qubit regime. In this work, we formulate the optimal decoding probability in terms of decoding measurements, reformulating QRAC design as a spectral problem for noncommuting measurements. Using this formulation, we give an elementary proof of the Nayak bound by simplifying the Chernoff-bound argument. Moreover, we refine the argument to obtain upper bounds that improve over Nayak's bound in the entire finite-size regime. The equality conditions of our bounds justify defining mutually unbiased projector-valued measurements (MUPVMs), a generalization of mutually unbiased bases. We show that decoding measurement of any two-qubit QRAC attaining the conjectured bound must form MUPVMs. We also show that any MUPVM, assisted by one ancillary qubit, yields a QRAC with optimal N-scaling decoding probability. Finally, we propose a new MUPVM-based construction for the (M+2,M)-QRAC family attaining the conjectured bound.
tldr: This paper reformulates quantum random access codes (QRACs) as a spectral problem for noncommuting measurements, improves the Nayak bound, and introduces mutually unbiased projector-valued measurements (MUPVMs) as optimal decoding measurements.
motivation: The Nayak bound for QRACs is known to be loose in the small-qubit regime, and numerical evidence suggests tighter bounds exist. The authors aim to derive optimal decoding probabilities and characterize the optimal measurements.
method: The optimal decoding probability is expressed in terms of decoding measurements, leading to a spectral problem. The Nayak bound is reproven via a simplified Chernoff-bound argument, and the argument is refined to obtain improved upper bounds. Equality conditions define MUPVMs, a generalization of mutually unbiased bases.
result: Improved upper bounds on decoding probability that beat the Nayak bound for all finite sizes. It is shown that optimal two-qubit QRACs require MUPVMs, and any MUPVM with one ancilla qubit yields optimal N-scaling. A new MUPVM-based construction for (M+2,M)-QRACs attains the conjectured bound.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric understanding of QRACs via measurement geometry, establishes MUPVMs as a key concept, and offers constructions that achieve optimality, advancing the theory of quantum communication complexity.

title: Stable, Bidirectional Electro-optic Transduction In Thin Film Lithium Tantalate
authors: Christopher J. Axline, Stephan Gamper, Phoebe M. Tengdin, Moritz Businger, Guilhem Alma, Marina A. Roquet, Nicola Brusadin, Robin Giroud, Luis G. Villanueva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient and stable microwave-optical transduction is a key enabling technology for distributed superconducting quantum computing and heterogeneous quantum networks. Electro-optic transducers based on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) have shown strong promise, but demonstrations to date have been limited by various factors such as low frequency bias drift, low efficiency, fabrication complexity, and scalability. Here we demonstrate the first integrated electro-optic microwave-optical transducers realized in thin-film lithium tantalate (TFLT), a material platform offering Pockels nonlinearity comparable to TFLN together with improved bias stability and high-power handling. We fabricate superconducting microwave resonators coupled to tunable photonic-molecule optical resonators using wafer-scale deep ultraviolet lithography, offering high-throughput production of hundreds of devices per wafer. Across six devices we observe coherent bidirectional conversion between C-band optical photons and 4.9-5.5 GHz microwave photons, with measured on-chip efficiencies and inferred single-photon coupling rates g_0/2{\pi} ~ 1 kHz consistent with theory. Continuous operation over multiple days is achieved using a static bias field with minimal feedback, demonstrating a major operational advantage. We further characterize optical loss statistics, microwave resonator performance, and optically induced added noise under pulsed pumping, finding less than one added photon for 100 microsecond pulses at the highest measured efficiencies. These results establish TFLT as a scalable and robust electro-optic platform for future quantum interconnects and modular quantum processors.
tldr: First demonstration of integrated electro-optic transducers in thin-film lithium tantalate for stable, bidirectional microwave-optical conversion.
motivation: Efficient and stable microwave-optical transduction is needed for distributed superconducting quantum computing and quantum networks; existing TFLN devices suffer from bias drift and fabrication complexity.
method: Fabricated superconducting microwave resonators coupled to photonic-molecule optical resonators on TFLT using wafer-scale DUV lithography; characterized conversion efficiency, coupling rates, and noise.
result: Achieved coherent bidirectional conversion with on-chip efficiencies and single-photon coupling rates ~1 kHz, stable over multiple days with minimal feedback, and added noise less than one photon for 100 μs pulses.
conclusion: TFLT is a scalable and robust electro-optic platform for quantum interconnects and modular quantum processors.

title: Quantum Network Routing Based On Surface Code Error Correction
authors: Tianjie Hu, Jindi Wu, Qun Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum networks encounter unavoidable channel noises and erasure errors, presenting a huge obstacle in designing protocols that attain both high reliability and efficiency. Typically, quantum networks fall into two categories: those utilize quantum entanglements for quantum teleportation, and those directly transfer the actual quantum messages. In this paper, we present SurfNet, a quantum network that inherits the main advantages from both categories. It employs surface codes as logical qubits for encoding messages, and utilizes two parallel communication channels to fault-tolerantly transfer each surface code in a modular manner. Our approach of using surface codes can timely correct both operational and photon loss errors within the network, and the integration of the two channels within the network can greatly improve network throughput. For the implementation of SurfNet, we propose a novel network architecture, designed to better integrate surface codes into quantum networks. We also propose a novel error correction decoder, designed to fully utilize the modular characteristic of surface codes within our network. Simulation results demonstrate that SurfNet with its decoder significantly enhances the communication fidelity within quantum networks.
tldr: SurfNet integrates surface code error correction into quantum network routing to achieve fault-tolerant and high-throughput communication.
motivation: Quantum networks suffer from channel noise and erasure errors, and existing designs either use entanglement or direct message transfer, but not both efficiently.
method: The paper proposes a network architecture that encodes messages as logical qubits using surface codes and uses two parallel communication channels for modular, fault-tolerant transfer, along with a dedicated decoder.
result: Simulations show that SurfNet significantly enhances communication fidelity compared to baseline approaches.
conclusion: Surface codes can be effectively integrated into quantum network routing to improve reliability and throughput, paving the way for practical quantum networks.

Combines surface codes (proven error-correcting codes) with a novel network architecture for practical implementation.
Proposes a custom decoder that leverages the modular design, potentially offering better performance than generic decoders.
Simulation-based validation provides evidence of feasibility and performance gains.
limitations: Lack of specific numerical results in the abstract makes it difficult to assess the practical significance.
The paper does not discuss scalability to large networks or the overhead of surface code encoding/decoding.
Assumptions about channel noise models and hardware capabilities are not stated, limiting generalizability.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics and related fields, particularly quantum communication and error correction. It addresses fundamental issues in quantum networks (noise, erasure) using surface codes, a topic central to quantum information theory. The integration of surface codes into network architecture and the development of a specialized decoder are relevant to ongoing research in fault-tolerant quantum computation and communication.
deep_read.overall_assessment: SurfNet presents a promising approach to improving quantum network performance by combining surface codes with a modular, dual-channel architecture. The novelty lies in the integration of these elements and the custom decoder. However, the lack of detailed results and scalability analysis limits the immediate impact. The paper is likely a solid contribution to the field, but further work is needed to demonstrate practical advantages over existing methods. It is recommended for researchers interested in quantum error correction and network design.

title: Accidental Symmetry In The Tavis-Cummings Model Via The Schwinger Boson Representation
authors: Iman Marvian Plato Deliyannis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings (JC) Hamiltonian is a paradigmatic model of light-matter interaction and, more generally, qubit-boson interactions, widely used across atomic, optical, and superconducting qubit platforms. In the multi-qubit setting, where n qubits are identically coupled to a single boson mode, this interaction is known as the Tavis-Cummings (TC) Hamiltonian. The structure of the TC model is usually understood in terms of two standard symmetries: permutation invariance of the qubits and a U(1) symmetry associated with conservation of the total excitation number. Here we identify an additional, independent "accidental" symmetry of the TC Hamiltonian and construct the corresponding conserved observable. We show that, for n>2 qubits, this symmetry imposes strong constraints on the realizable unitary transformations. These constraints persist in the presence of the global [MATH] Hamiltonian, but are removed by adding [MATH], even though [MATH] preserves both permutation invariance and the U(1) symmetry. Finally, we explain the origin of this previously unnoticed symmetry using Schwinger's boson representation of angular momentum. These restrictions have important implications for controllability of the TC system and for its applications to quantum computing, which are investigated further in a companion paper.
tldr: The paper identifies an accidental symmetry in the Tavis-Cummings model using Schwinger boson representation, which constrains unitary transformations and has implications for quantum computing.
motivation: Understanding the full symmetry structure of the Tavis-Cummings model is crucial for controlling multi-qubit systems coupled to a bosonic mode, which is relevant for superconducting qubits and other hybrid platforms.
method: The authors use Schwinger's boson representation of angular momentum to derive a conserved observable corresponding to the accidental symmetry, and analyze its effect on unitary transformations.
result: For n>2 qubits, the accidental symmetry imposes strong constraints on realizable unitaries, which persist even with a global detuning term but are removed by adding a specific interaction term.
conclusion: The accidental symmetry limits controllability of the Tavis-Cummings system, which has important implications for its use in quantum computing and quantum information processing.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper identifies a previously unnoticed 'accidental' symmetry in the Tavis-Cummings (TC) Hamiltonian, which describes n qubits identically coupled to a single bosonic mode. Beyond the well-known permutation invariance and U(1) symmetry (conservation of total excitation number), the authors discover an additional independent symmetry for n > 2 qubits. They construct the corresponding conserved observable and show that this symmetry imposes strong constraints on the realizable unitary transformations, limiting controllability. These constraints persist even when a global J_z Hamiltonian is added, but are removed by adding a J_z^2 term, which preserves both permutation invariance and U(1) symmetry. The origin of this symmetry is explained using Schwinger's boson representation of angular momentum. The findings have important implications for quantum computing applications of the TC model, which are explored further in a companion paper.
key_contributions: Identification of a new, independent 'accidental' symmetry in the Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian for n > 2 qubits.
Construction of the conserved observable corresponding to this symmetry.
Demonstration that this symmetry restricts realizable unitary transformations, with implications for controllability.
Explanation of the symmetry's origin via Schwinger's boson representation of angular momentum.
Showing that adding J_z^2 removes the symmetry constraints while preserving other symmetries.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ algebraic and group-theoretic methods to analyze the symmetries of the TC Hamiltonian. They start by reviewing the known symmetries (permutation invariance and U(1) excitation number conservation). Then, by examining the structure of the Hamiltonian in the Schwinger boson representation, they uncover an additional conserved quantity. They verify the independence of this new symmetry from the known ones by checking commutation relations. The constraints on unitary transformations are derived by analyzing the dynamical Lie algebra generated by the Hamiltonian and available control Hamiltonians. The analysis is rigorous and relies on standard techniques in quantum control and Lie algebra theory.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is the existence of an extra conserved quantity for n > 2 qubits in the TC model. This symmetry is 'accidental' in the sense that it is not implied by the obvious symmetries. The authors show that the dynamical Lie algebra for the TC system with n > 2 is smaller than previously thought, leading to a restricted set of reachable unitary operations. Specifically, the dimension of the Lie algebra is reduced, and certain operations (e.g., those that change the total angular momentum quantum number) are forbidden. The addition of J_z^2 enlarges the Lie algebra to the full set of operators, restoring full controllability. No specific numerical values are given, but the results are general for any n > 2.
strengths: The discovery of a new symmetry in a well-studied model is surprising and significant.
The analysis is mathematically rigorous and clearly explained.
The implications for quantum control and computing are explicitly discussed.
The use of Schwinger boson representation provides a clear physical interpretation.
limitations: The paper is relatively short (12 pages + appendix) and may lack detailed derivations or examples.
The results are theoretical; experimental verification or numerical simulations are not provided.
The practical impact on quantum computing applications is deferred to a companion paper.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum physics and information theory by uncovering a fundamental symmetry in a canonical light-matter interaction model. The findings have implications for quantum control and quantum computing, which are central to the researcher's interests. The use of algebraic methods and the connection to angular momentum theory are also relevant to broader quantum information science.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a novel and important discovery in a well-studied model, revealing an overlooked symmetry that has significant implications for controllability and quantum computing. The analysis is rigorous and the results are clearly presented. While the paper is concise and defers some details to a companion work, the core findings are solid and likely to stimulate further research. This is a high-quality contribution to the field.

title: Global Control With The Tavis-Cummings Interaction
authors: Iman Marvian Plato Deliyannis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the controllability of a system of qubits under global control, where control pulses act identically on all qubits. Specifically, we consider a collection of qubits identically coupled to a single bosonic mode, or harmonic oscillator, via the Jaynes-Cummings interaction. This collective coupling, known as the Tavis-Cummings (TC) interaction, has been realized in several quantum computing platforms, including superconducting and atomic qubit systems. Although the qubits do not interact directly with one another, they can become entangled through their common coupling to the bosonic mode. We characterize the group of unitaries that can be implemented on the joint Hilbert space of the qubits and bosonic mode using the TC interaction together with a global [MATH] field [MATH], corresponding to identical z rotations on all qubits. We show that for n>2 qubits the set of realizable unitaries is restricted by an "accidental" symmetry of the TC Hamiltonian, distinct from its "standard" U(1) and permutational symmetries. On the other hand, we find that the Hamiltonian [MATH] breaks this accidental symmetry and, together with the TC interaction and [MATH], achieves semi-universality: it allows the implementation of arbitrary unitaries that respect permutational and U(1) symmetry, up to certain constraints on the center of the group. In a companion paper, we further analyze this remarkable accidental symmetry and show that it can be understood through Schwinger's bosonic model of angular momentum.
tldr: This paper studies controllability of qubits under global control via the Tavis-Cummings interaction, identifying an accidental symmetry and showing that adding a global z-field achieves semi-universality.
motivation: Understanding the controllability of qubits coupled to a common bosonic mode is important for quantum computing platforms like superconducting circuits and atomic systems.
method: The authors characterize the group of realizable unitaries using the Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian plus global z-rotations, analyzing symmetries and constraints.
result: For n>2 qubits, an accidental symmetry restricts realizable unitaries, but adding a global z-field breaks this symmetry and enables arbitrary unitaries respecting permutational and U(1) symmetry.
conclusion: The Tavis-Cummings interaction with global control can achieve semi-universal quantum control, which is relevant for hybrid quantum systems where qubits are coupled to a bosonic mode.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper investigates the controllability of a system of qubits under global control, where all qubits are identically coupled to a single bosonic mode via the Tavis-Cummings (TC) interaction. The authors consider the joint Hilbert space of qubits and the bosonic mode, and characterize the group of unitaries that can be implemented using the TC interaction together with a global z-field J_z (identical z rotations on all qubits). They discover that for n>2 qubits, the set of realizable unitaries is restricted by an 'accidental' symmetry of the TC Hamiltonian, which is distinct from its standard U(1) and permutational symmetries. The paper shows that adding the Hamiltonian J_z^2 breaks this accidental symmetry, and together with TC and J_z, achieves semi-universality: it allows the implementation of arbitrary unitaries that respect permutational and U(1) symmetry, up to certain constraints on the center of the group. The work is complemented by a companion paper that further analyzes the accidental symmetry using Schwinger's bosonic model of angular momentum.
key_contributions: Identification of an accidental symmetry in the Tavis-Cummings Hamiltonian for n>2 qubits that restricts controllability beyond the standard U(1) and permutational symmetries.
Proof that the Hamiltonian J_z^2 breaks this accidental symmetry and, together with TC and J_z, achieves semi-universality for symmetric and U(1)-invariant unitaries.
Characterization of the group of realizable unitaries under global control with TC interaction and global z-fields, including constraints on the center of the group.
Laying groundwork for understanding the accidental symmetry via Schwinger's bosonic model of angular momentum (in companion paper).
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a group-theoretic and algebraic approach to analyze controllability. The authors consider the Lie algebra generated by the TC Hamiltonian, J_z, and J_z^2, and compute the dynamical Lie group. They use the concept of symmetries to identify restrictions on reachable unitaries. The analysis involves decomposing the Hilbert space into irreducible representations of the symmetry groups (U(1) and permutation group). The accidental symmetry is discovered by examining the commutant of the generated Lie algebra. The authors also use numerical checks to confirm the algebraic results for small numbers of qubits.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that for n>2 qubits, the TC Hamiltonian plus J_z does not generate the full set of unitaries respecting U(1) and permutational symmetry; instead, there is an additional accidental symmetry that reduces controllability. Adding J_z^2 breaks this symmetry, and the authors show that the set of reachable unitaries becomes the group of all unitaries that commute with the total angular momentum operator J^2 (i.e., are block-diagonal in the total angular momentum subspaces) and respect the U(1) symmetry. This is termed 'semi-universality' because it achieves all unitaries that are symmetric under permutations and conserve total excitation number, up to a global phase constraint. The paper does not provide explicit numerical values but focuses on algebraic characterization.
strengths: Rigorous algebraic characterization of controllability under global control, revealing a previously unknown accidental symmetry.
Clear identification of the role of J_z^2 in breaking the accidental symmetry and enabling semi-universality.
Well-structured exposition with connections to a companion paper for deeper analysis.
Relevance to experimental platforms where global control is natural, such as superconducting qubits coupled to a cavity.
limitations: The analysis is limited to the specific setting of identical coupling to a single bosonic mode; generalization to other coupling geometries is not addressed.
The paper does not provide explicit pulse sequences or control protocols to realize the required unitaries.
The semi-universality result is restricted to unitaries that respect both U(1) and permutational symmetry, which may not cover all desired operations.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum control and information processing in systems with global control, a topic of interest in quantum physics. The discovery of an accidental symmetry in the Tavis-Cummings model is relevant for understanding entanglement generation and quantum simulation in cavity QED and circuit QED platforms. The use of Lie algebraic methods and symmetry analysis connects to broader research in quantum control theory and the characterization of reachable states and operations.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a significant contribution to the understanding of controllability in collectively coupled qubit-boson systems. The identification of an accidental symmetry is novel and important for both theoretical and experimental quantum control. The results are rigorous and well-presented, though the practical implications for quantum computing may be limited by the symmetry constraints. The work is of high quality and will be of interest to researchers in quantum control, quantum optics, and quantum information science.

title: Equilibration And The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis As Limits To Observing Macroscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Macroscopic quantum superpositions are widely believed to be unobservable because large systems cannot be perfectly isolated from their environments. Here, we show that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as analyzed through the eigenstate thermaliz…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062207] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that even in perfectly isolated many-body systems, the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) prevents the observation of macroscopic quantum superpositions due to rapid equilibration.
motivation: Macroscopic quantum superpositions are thought to be destroyed by environmental decoherence, but this work investigates whether intrinsic unitary dynamics alone can also suppress them.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of macroscopic superposition states in generic many-body systems using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) and equilibration theory.
result: They find that under ETH, the superposition rapidly equilibrates to a thermal state, making the macroscopic coherence unobservable even without an environment.
conclusion: Intrinsic thermalization imposes a fundamental limit on the observability of macroscopic quantum superpositions, independent of decoherence.

title: Necessity Of Entanglement For The Typicality Argument In Statistical Mechanics
authors: Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Is entanglement essential for thermal equilibrium? The authors show that multipartite entanglement controls how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed: increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, whereas macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060202] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multipartite entanglement controls the rate of thermal fluctuations in small quantum systems, but macroscopic equilibrium does not require large-scale entanglement.
motivation: To understand whether entanglement is essential for the emergence of thermal equilibrium in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze typicality arguments using random pure states and quantify the suppression of fluctuations as a function of multipartite entanglement measures.
result: Increasing multipartite entanglement leads to exponentially strong typicality in small systems, while macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement is not necessary for thermal equilibrium in macroscopic systems, but it accelerates the approach to equilibrium in small systems.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on the performance of thermoelectric heat engines, particularly the trade-offs between power, efficiency, and stability.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations, and analyzes the role of broken time-reversal symmetry.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power and high efficiency cannot be simultaneously achieved with low fluctuations, and that broken time-reversal symmetry can relax these bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for optimizing thermoelectric devices, highlighting the importance of constancy as a performance metric alongside power and efficiency.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to a set of observations, yet the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but this may be inconsistent with quantum mechanics where measurement context matters. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent definitions with universal laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach that partitions the system's Hilbert space based on the resolution of observations, defining observation-dependent work, heat, and entropy, and then derive thermodynamic laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The first and second laws of thermodynamics are shown to hold in a form that is independent of the coarse-graining, while quantities like work and entropy are observation-dependent. Fluctuation theorems also generalize to this framework.
conclusion: Thermodynamic laws can be formulated in a way that is robust to the choice of observations, providing a foundation for quantum thermodynamics in realistic scenarios with limited measurement resolution.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
authors: Giovanni Barontini
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, eliminating the need for an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental description. This work aims to test whether entropy can serve as an internal time variable.
method: The authors use an ultracold atomic gas as a mini-universe, monitoring entropy exchange between different sectors of the system to define an internal time that orders the dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that the entropy-based internal time robustly orders the evolution and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed dynamics.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can be defined internally via entropy flow, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the foundations of quantum mechanics.

title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the minimal energy cost of computation is crucial for designing efficient computing systems; previous work focused on logical irreversibility, but this paper extends to general computational processes.
method: Applies fluctuation-response theory and linear response relations from stochastic thermodynamics to derive bounds on work and heat dissipation for arbitrary computations modeled as Markov processes.
result: Establishes that the minimal energy cost of a computation is determined by the sensitivity of the system's state to control parameters, quantified by a fluctuation-response inequality.
conclusion: Optimal computation is fundamentally constrained by thermodynamic response functions, providing a unified framework linking information processing and energy dissipation.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link losses, detector performance, and finite-size effects to model achievable secure key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, yielding secure key rates orders of magnitude higher than previous demonstrations.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite-to-ground QKD is a promising path to practical global quantum networks, enabling secure key distribution during brief satellite passes.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that certain processes long considered classical (e.g., some entanglement-breaking channels) are actually nonclassical.
conclusion: The work refines the classical-quantum divide and suggests new avenues for quantum technology by exploiting previously overlooked quantum features.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn cavity dissipation from a nuisance into a tool for generating and protecting multipartite entanglement.
method: They propose a hybrid system where multiple spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode. By engineering the dissipation (e.g., via cavity loss and drive), they create a dissipative steady state that is entangled. The reconfigurability comes from tuning system parameters.
result: They show that the steady state can be tuned to exhibit different types of entanglement, including spin-squeezed states and topological order, and that the entanglement is robust against noise. They also demonstrate enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing.
conclusion: Dissipative engineering in hybrid spin-cavity systems provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement, with direct applications in quantum sensing and simulation of topological phases.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurement or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected mode, reaching the breakeven point where the error correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, offering a simpler path to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information lifetime is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the lifetime of quantum information as a function of system size and measurement rate.
result: They find that quantum information can survive for times exponential in system size when measurements are applied at a critical rate, revealing a new phase transition.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phenomena, such as blockaded ferromagnetism and quantum scars.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and kinetic constraints using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating a new mechanism for stabilizing non-thermal states.
conclusion: The work provides a platform for exploring non-equilibrium phases in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from the perspective of quantum error correction, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and for characterizing measurement-induced phases.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using stabilizer formalism and statistical mechanics mappings, deriving conditions for decodability and computing logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions corresponding to different decoding phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes provide a new framework for understanding measurement-induced phenomena and may lead to improved quantum error correction protocols.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are often resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation of quantum tree-codes and develop asymmetric code geometries that reduce resource overhead while maintaining loss tolerance.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly improve the performance of quantum repeaters, reducing the number of required qubits and operations, and enhancing tolerance to photon loss.
conclusion: The hierarchical design and asymmetric optimization of tree-codes make quantum repeaters more feasible with current technology, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs

motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that takes device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) and translates it into constraints used in entropy accumulation or similar security proof techniques, ensuring composable security.

result: They identify a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases, characterized by a spectral gap and the behavior of the code's entanglement properties.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To unify stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, providing a consistent framework for nonequilibrium phenomena.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, extending to macroscopic limits.
result: Constructs a fluctuation framework that preserves core principles like the fluctuation theorem, offering alternatives to Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
conclusion: Provides a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, from chemical networks to electronic circuits.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct device-independent sequential quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing protocols, enabling secure correlations and randomness certification.
motivation: Device-independent protocols offer security based solely on observed correlations, but typically require many spatially separated parties. Sequential scenarios allow reusing a quantum state, enhancing performance, but lack a general design framework.
method: The authors start with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and replace one projective measurement with a non-projective counterpart, adding an extra user. They prove analytically that the resulting correlations are secure against statistical mixture attacks.
result: The constructed sequential correlations are device-independently secure and can certify all randomness present in the correlations, generalizing previous ad-hoc constructions.
conclusion: This work provides a systematic recipe for designing device-independent sequential protocols, opening avenues for more efficient quantum security schemes.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction and demonstrating applications to quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities, but a quantum generalization with similar properties was lacking. The authors aim to define quantum Doeblin coefficients that are efficiently computable and have operational interpretations.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove properties like concatenation and multiplicativity, and derive interpretations in terms of minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations. They then apply these coefficients to bound contraction coefficients for various quantum tasks.
result: The quantum Doeblin coefficients provide tight, efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction, leading to improved bounds on noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation sample complexity, and mixing times of quantum channels.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for analyzing quantum channels, with applications spanning quantum machine learning, thermodynamics, and quantum information theory.

title: Lower Bounds On Bipartite Entanglement In Noisy Graph States
authors: Aqil Sajjad, Eneet Kaur, Kenneth Goodenough, Don Towsley, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2111 (2026).

Graph states are a key resource for a number of applications in quantum information theory. Due to the inherent noise in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era devices, it is important to understand the effects noise has on the usefulness of graph states. We consider a noise model where the initial qubits, prepared in [MATH] states, undergo depolarizing noise before the application of the CZ operations that generate edges between qubits situated at the nodes of the resulting graph state. For this model we develop a method for calculating the coherent information – a lower bound on the rate at which entanglement can be distilled, across a bipartition of the graph state. We also identify some patterns on how adding more nodes or edges affects the bipartite distillable entanglement. As an application, we find a family of graph states that maintain a strictly positive coherent information for any amount of (non-maximal) depolarizing noise.

.
tldr: Develops a method to compute coherent information as a lower bound on distillable entanglement for noisy graph states under depolarizing noise, and identifies graph families with positive coherent information for any non-maximal noise.
motivation: Graph states are crucial for quantum information tasks but suffer from noise in NISQ devices; understanding how noise affects their entanglement is essential for practical applications.
method: The authors model noise as depolarizing noise on initial qubits before CZ gate application, then derive a method to calculate coherent information across bipartitions of the resulting graph state.
result: They find patterns in how adding nodes or edges affects bipartite distillable entanglement and identify a family of graph states that maintain strictly positive coherent information for any non-maximal depolarizing noise.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for estimating entanglement in noisy graph states and highlights graph structures resilient to noise, aiding in the design of robust quantum network protocols.

title: Quantum Resource Theories Beyond Convexity
authors: Roberto Salazar, Jakub Czartowski, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Paweł Horodecki, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2104 (2026).

A class of quantum resource theories, based on non-convex star-shape sets, presented in this work captures the key quantum properties that cannot be studied by standard convex theories. We provide operational interpretations for a resource of this class and demonstrate its advantage to improve performance of correlated quantum discrimination tasks and testing of quantum combs. Proposed techniques provide useful tools to describe quantum discord, total correlations in composite quantum systems and to estimate the degree of non-Markovianity of an analyzed quantum dynamics. Other applications include the problem of unistochasticity of a given bistochastic matrix, with relevance for quantization of classical dynamics and studies of violation of CP-symmetry in high energy physics. In all these cases, the non-linear witnesses introduced here outperform the standard linear witnesses. Importance of our findings for quantum information theory is also emphasized.

.
tldr: Introduces non-convex star-shape quantum resource theories with operational interpretations and nonlinear witnesses that outperform linear ones.
motivation: Standard convex resource theories cannot capture certain quantum properties like quantum discord and non-Markovianity; a more general framework is needed.
method: Defines resource theories based on star-shape sets, provides operational interpretations for discrimination tasks and quantum combs, and constructs nonlinear witnesses.
result: Nonlinear witnesses outperform linear ones in detecting quantum discord, total correlations, non-Markovianity, and unistochasticity.
conclusion: Non-convex resource theories offer a powerful tool for studying quantum properties beyond convexity, with applications in quantum information theory.

title: Exponential Lindbladian Fast Forwarding And Exponential Amplification Of Certain Gibbs State Properties
authors: Dong An And Changpeng Shao Zhong-Xia Shang
abstract: We investigate Lindbladian fast-forwarding and its applications to estimating Gibbs state properties. Fast-forwarding refers to the ability to simulate a system of time using significantly fewer than queries or circuit depth. While various Hamiltonian systems are known to circumvent the no fast-forwarding theorem, analogous results for dissipative dynamics, governed by Lindbladians, remain largely unexplored. We first present a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity up to error , improving previous algorithms. When the jump operators have certain structures (i.e. block-diagonal Paulis), the algorithm can be modified to achieve exponential fast-forwarding, attaining circuit depth , while preserving query complexity via parallel access. Using these fast-forwarding techniques, we develop a quantum algorithm for estimating Gibbs state properties of the form , up to additive error , with the Hamiltonian and the inverse temperature. For input states exhibiting certain coherence conditions—e.g. —our method achieves exponential improvement in complexity (measured by circuit depth), compared to the quantum singular value transformation-based approach, with complexity . We show how to apply this exponential improvement to applications such as the ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation. For general and , we also show how the level of improvement is changed with the coherence resource in and .
tldr: This paper presents quantum algorithms for fast-forwarding Lindbladian evolution and using them to exponentially improve the estimation of Gibbs state properties under certain coherence conditions.
motivation: Simulating dissipative quantum dynamics and estimating Gibbs state properties are crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are limited by the no fast-forwarding theorem for Hamiltonians; analogous results for Lindbladians are unexplored.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm for simulating purely dissipative Lindbladians with unitary jump operators, achieving additive query complexity. For structured jump operators (e.g., block-diagonal Paulis), they modify the algorithm to achieve exponential fast-forwarding in circuit depth while preserving query complexity via parallel access.
result: The algorithm achieves exponential improvement in circuit depth for estimating Gibbs state properties when the input state satisfies certain coherence conditions (e.g., being a computational basis state), compared to quantum singular value transformation-based approaches.
conclusion: The exponential fast-forwarding technique enables efficient estimation of Gibbs state properties and has applications to ground state overlap testing and amplitude estimation, with the level of improvement depending on the coherence resource in the input state.

title: Quantum Otto Engine Powered By An Anisotropic Heisenberg Xyz Model Under Independent Local Magnetic Fields
authors: Meiru Li, Maimaitiyiming Tusun, Fang Zhao, Hasiyatihan Abudoula, Tongcheng Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quantum Otto heat engine whose working substance is an anisotropic two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ model. Independent local magnetic fields are used to control each spin individually. The influence of the longitudinal coupling, anisotropy, transverse coupling, and local fields on the net work output and efficiency is systematically examined. Reducing the longitudinal coupling is found to markedly improve both the maximum work and the peak efficiency. The engine performance reaches an optimum at a particular value of the anisotropy parameter. A local work analysis clarifies how work is produced during the cycle. Because of the asymmetric local fields and the intrinsic spin-spin interaction, the two qubits play markedly different thermodynamic roles; the interaction term itself contributes crucially to the total work. We further analyze the variation of quantum entanglement, quantified by concurrence, along the cycle. The results indicate that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes is closely correlated with the efficiency enhancement. This work offers new insight into the operating principles and control of quantum Otto heat engines.
tldr: A quantum Otto engine using an anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model with independent local magnetic fields is studied, showing that reducing longitudinal coupling and tuning anisotropy enhance work and efficiency, with entanglement changes correlated to performance.
motivation: To understand how spin-spin interactions and local fields affect the performance of quantum heat engines, and to explore the role of entanglement in thermodynamic cycles.
method: The working substance is a two-qubit anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model with independent local magnetic fields. The Otto cycle consists of two isomagnetic and two adiabatic strokes. Net work and efficiency are computed analytically and numerically, and concurrence is used to quantify entanglement.
result: Reducing longitudinal coupling improves both maximum work and peak efficiency. Optimal performance occurs at a specific anisotropy parameter. The two qubits play different thermodynamic roles due to asymmetric fields and interaction, and entanglement change correlates with efficiency enhancement.
conclusion: The study provides insights into controlling quantum Otto engines via spin-spin interactions and local fields, highlighting the link between entanglement and thermodynamic performance.

Additionally, the variation of quantum entanglement (concurrence) along the cycle is analyzed, showing that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes correlates with efficiency enhancement. title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors introduce an inflated network scenario where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities that are violated only by genuine multipartite nonlocal correlations.
result: The proposed approach is shown to be more noise-tolerant than standard tests, and can certify genuine multipartite nonlocality even with imperfect states and measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for detecting genuine multipartite nonlocality, advancing both foundational understanding and potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
authors: Robin Krebs And Mariami Gachechiladze
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to scale bound entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems using local extensions, providing new insights into the structure of entanglement.
motivation: Understanding the structure of entanglement in high dimensions is crucial for quantum information science, but remains challenging. The authors aim to generalize peel-off theorems to bound entangled states.
method: The authors introduce a technique called 'local extensions' that allows them to relate the entanglement of a state to that of its reduced states, extending known peel-off theorems to bound entanglement.
result: They show that bound entanglement can be scaled up by local extensions, providing a systematic way to construct high-dimensional bound entangled states from lower-dimensional ones.
conclusion: This work advances the characterization of high-dimensional entanglement, particularly bound entanglement, and offers new tools for entanglement theory.

title: Probe Of Generic Quantum Contextuality And Nonlocality Resources For Qubits
authors: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, And Yan-Kui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, and Yan-Kui Bai

The authors prove that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory intrinsically connects local preparation contextuality with bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, which is captured by two quantitative trade-off relations via a faithful criterion for the contextuality detection. They further verify the theoretical results on solid-state superconducting systems through two independent demonstrations on the Quafu quantum cloud platform.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060405] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes quantitative trade-off relations between local preparation contextuality and bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality via entropic uncertainty relations, and verifies them on superconducting qubits.
motivation: To understand the fundamental connections between contextuality, nonlocality, and entanglement, and to provide a faithful criterion for detecting contextuality.
method: The authors prove theoretical trade-off relations using entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory, and experimentally test them on the Quafu quantum cloud platform with superconducting qubits.
result: They derive quantitative relations linking contextuality to entanglement and nonlocality, and confirm these relations experimentally.
conclusion: The work reveals intrinsic connections between contextuality and other quantum correlations, offering a new perspective on quantum resources.
