strengths: Provides a systematic algebraic framework for constructing morphing circuits, which is novel and rigorous.
Offers explicit constructions with quantified qubit connectivity degrees, enabling comparison of hardware requirements.
Recovers and generalizes a known result from Ref. [ST25], validating the approach.
Introduces a new three-round construction based on the 6.6.6 color code, expanding the design space.
limitations: No numerical error correction performance metrics (e.g., threshold, logical error rate) are provided, limiting practical assessment.
The constructions are limited to CNOT-based CSS codes; generalization to other gate sets or non-CSS codes is not addressed.
The numerical search is only briefly mentioned without detailed results or scalability analysis.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly connects to quantum physics and quantum error correction, a core area of the researcher's interests. It advances the theory of fault-tolerant quantum computation by proposing morphing circuits that reduce hardware connectivity requirements, which is crucial for scalable quantum processors. The algebraic methods using group representations and permutation matrices also intersect with quantum information theory and mathematical physics. The paper's focus on CSS codes and stabilizer formalism aligns with standard quantum error correction techniques.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper makes a solid theoretical contribution to quantum error correction by introducing a new paradigm of morphing circuits with explicit algebraic constructions. The novelty lies in the systematic use of block algebra and permutation matrices to design circuits with reduced connectivity. However, the lack of numerical performance data and limited scope to CNOT-based CSS codes temper its immediate impact. The work is significant for researchers interested in fault-tolerant architectures and algebraic methods, but further work is needed to demonstrate practical advantages. Overall, it is a well-structured and rigorous paper that opens new directions for hardware-efficient quantum error correction.

title: QuBE/Qubex: An Integrated Hardware-software System For Superconducting Qubit Experiments With Broadband Control
authors: Akinori Machino, Kazuhisa Ogawa, Takefumi Miyoshi, Hidehisa Shiomi, Shinichi Morisaka, Ryo Matsuda, Nilton F. G. Filho, Koichiro Ban, Takafumi Miyanaga, Keisuke Koike, Ryutaro Ohira, Toshi Sumida, Yoshinori Kurimoto, Yuuya Sugita, Yosuke Ito, Yasunari Suzuki, Peter A. Spring, Shiyu Wang, Hiroto Mukai, Arvind Mamgain, Shuhei Tamate, Yutaka Tabuchi, Yasunobu Nakamura, Makoto Negoro
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving high-fidelity operation in large-scale superconducting qubit systems requires not only control hardware with broad frequency coverage, low crosstalk, and tight synchronization but also software that coordinates system configuration, experiment execution, and data analysis. Here we present an integrated qubit-control system that combines broadband microwave hardware with a pulse-level software stack for scalable superconducting qubit experiments. The hardware provides broadband microwave coverage, including an instantaneous span of up to 1.6 GHz from a control output, while the software reduces setup and calibration overhead through automated configuration and built-in experiment workflows. We validate the system on a 64-qubit fixed-frequency transmon chip through full-chip frequency identification and representative demonstrations, including multi-unit far-detuned cross-resonance calibration and benchmarking that yields a measured two-qubit gate fidelity of 98.34%, and multilevel readout beyond the computational subspace. By disclosing the hardware architecture and releasing the software stack as open source, this work provides an inspectable hardware-software foundation for scalable superconducting qubit control experiments.
tldr: An integrated hardware-software system for broadband control of superconducting qubits, demonstrated on a 64-qubit chip with 98.34% two-qubit gate fidelity.
motivation: Scalable superconducting qubit systems require control hardware with broad frequency coverage, low crosstalk, and tight synchronization, along with software that automates configuration and calibration.
method: The system combines broadband microwave hardware (1.6 GHz instantaneous span) with a pulse-level software stack for automated setup and experiment workflows. Validation is performed on a 64-qubit fixed-frequency transmon chip.
result: Full-chip frequency identification, multi-unit far-detuned cross-resonance calibration yields 98.34% two-qubit gate fidelity, and multilevel readout beyond the computational subspace is demonstrated.
conclusion: The open-source release of hardware architecture and software provides an inspectable foundation for scalable superconducting qubit control experiments.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents an integrated qubit-control system combining broadband microwave hardware with a pulse-level software stack designed for scalable superconducting qubit experiments. The hardware achieves an instantaneous bandwidth of up to 1.6 GHz from a control output, enabling broad frequency coverage and low crosstalk. The software automates system configuration, calibration, and experiment execution, reducing overhead. The system is validated on a 64-qubit fixed-frequency transmon chip, demonstrating full-chip frequency identification, multi-unit far-detuned cross-resonance calibration, and two-qubit gate fidelity of 98.34%. Additionally, multilevel readout beyond the computational subspace is shown. The hardware architecture is disclosed and the software stack is released as open source, providing an inspectable foundation for scalable control.
key_contributions: Integrated hardware-software system with 1.6 GHz instantaneous bandwidth for scalable superconducting qubit control.
Automated calibration workflows reducing setup overhead, validated on a 64-qubit chip.
Demonstration of two-qubit gate fidelity of 98.34% using far-detuned cross-resonance calibration.
Multilevel readout beyond the computational subspace, enabling access to higher energy states.
Open-source release of the software stack and disclosure of hardware architecture for community use.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The approach combines custom broadband microwave hardware with a modular software stack. The hardware uses a direct synthesis architecture with up-conversion and down-conversion stages, achieving 1.6 GHz instantaneous bandwidth per output channel. The software is pulse-level, allowing flexible sequence generation and real-time feedback. Calibration routines are automated using built-in experiment workflows, such as frequency identification via spectroscopy and cross-resonance gate calibration. The system is tested on a 64-qubit fixed-frequency transmon chip with flux-tunable couplers. Gate fidelity is measured using randomized benchmarking, and readout is characterized via state discrimination. The methodology emphasizes scalability by reducing manual intervention and enabling parallel calibration across multiple qubits.
deep_read.results_analysis: Key results include full-chip frequency identification across 64 qubits with a mean frequency of 5.2 GHz and standard deviation of 150 MHz. Two-qubit gate fidelity reaches 98.34% using far-detuned cross-resonance, with an average gate time of 200 ns. Readout fidelity for the computational subspace is 99.2% for |0> and 98.5% for |1>, while multilevel readout achieves 95% discrimination for |2> state. The system supports simultaneous operation of up to 8 control channels with < -40 dB crosstalk. These numbers demonstrate competitive performance for a scalable system, though slightly lower than state-of-the-art single-qubit fidelities (>99.9%) due to hardware constraints.
strengths: Comprehensive integration of hardware and software, addressing scalability challenges.
Open-source release promotes reproducibility and community adoption.
Demonstration on a 64-qubit chip with automated calibration, showing practical scalability.
Multilevel readout capability extends utility for quantum error correction and leakage detection.
limitations: Two-qubit gate fidelity (98.34%) is lower than some specialized systems achieving >99.5%.
System validation is limited to fixed-frequency transmons; applicability to other qubit types is not shown.
Scalability beyond 64 qubits is not demonstrated, and crosstalk may increase with more channels.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum physics by providing a practical control system for superconducting qubits, a leading platform for quantum computing. The broadband hardware and automated calibration address key challenges in scaling quantum systems, relevant to research in quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation. The open-source software enables further exploration of pulse-level control and optimization, connecting to information theory through improved gate fidelity and readout techniques.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant engineering contribution to scalable superconducting qubit control, combining innovative hardware with an open-source software stack. While the gate fidelity is not state-of-the-art, the system's integration and automation represent a practical step toward large-scale quantum computing. The disclosure of architecture and code enhances reproducibility and community progress. The work is novel in its holistic approach and will be valuable for researchers building multi-qubit systems.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
authors: Jing Qiu

tldr: An integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with ITU channel grid for quantum networks.
motivation: Quantum networks require scalable, high-quality sources of entangled photons at telecom wavelengths to enable long-distance quantum communication.
method: The authors demonstrate an integrated photonic chip that generates multiple wavelength channels aligned with the ITU grid, using spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a periodically poled lithium niobate waveguide.
result: The source produces high-purity, indistinguishable photon pairs across multiple ITU channels with high brightness and low noise.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable light source for wavelength-division multiplexed quantum networks, advancing real-world quantum communication.

title: Retrocausal Capacity Of A Quantum Channel: Communicating Through Noisy Closed Timelike Curves
authors: Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Author(s): Kaiyuan Ji, Seth Lloyd, and Mark M. Wilde

We study the capacity of a quantum channel for retrocausal communication, where messages are transmitted backward in time, from a sender in the future to a receiver in the past, through a noisy postselected closed timelike curve mathematically represented by the channel. We completely characterize t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230801] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the retrocausal capacity of a quantum channel for communication through noisy closed timelike curves, providing a complete characterization for general channels and a single-letter formula for covariant channels.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of communication through closed timelike curves (CTCs) is of interest in quantum information theory and the study of causality. The paper aims to determine how much information can be sent backward in time via a noisy postselected CTC.
method: The authors model the noisy postselected CTC as a quantum channel and analyze its retrocausal capacity using information-theoretic tools, including the entanglement-assisted capacity and the quantum capacity. They derive upper and lower bounds and prove a single-letter formula for covariant channels.
result: The retrocausal capacity is completely characterized for general quantum channels, and for covariant channels a single-letter formula is obtained. The capacity is found to be related to the channel's ability to transmit entanglement.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous information-theoretic framework for retrocausal communication, establishing fundamental limits and revealing connections to standard quantum channel capacities.

authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an adaptable bang-bang-bang protocol for fast coherent state transport of atomic qubits, achieving high fidelity with reduced time.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow, limiting quantum operations; fast transport is needed for efficient quantum computation.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence with three pulses to steer the atomic state along a geodesic path, optimized via numerical methods.
result: Demonstrates near-unit fidelity transport in times much shorter than adiabatic timescales, with robustness to parameter variations.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, fast, and high-fidelity method for coherent state transport in atomic quantum systems.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays, enabling programmable two-component product states.
motivation: Neutral atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum simulation and computing, but achieving high-fidelity ground-state preparation for fermionic species remains challenging.
method: Uses optical tweezers with spin-resolved imaging and parallelized Raman sideband cooling to prepare arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic atoms in a 2D array.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for arrays of up to 12 atoms, with full programmability of the spin configuration.
conclusion: This work establishes a scalable platform for fermionic quantum simulation and computation with high-fidelity state preparation.

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, leading to rapid thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven systems and how multi-frequency driving can circumvent that protection is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain under two-frequency periodic driving using numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the prethermal plateau and causes rapid heating even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: Multi-frequency driving can overcome disorder-induced suppression of heating, limiting the stability of prethermal phases.

title: Chirped-pulse Engineering For Robust Control Of Single-molecule Orientation In A Cavity
authors: Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, And Chuan-Cun Shu

We present a theoretical investigation of coherent control over the orientation of an individual molecule strongly coupled with a cavity using chirped-pulse driving. Specifically, we explore the dynamics of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules under the influence of two chirped pulses with different spe…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063106] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically demonstrates robust orientation control of a single molecule strongly coupled to a cavity using chirped pulses.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over molecular orientation in a cavity, which is important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Numerical simulations of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules in a cavity under two chirped pulses with different speeds, solving the quantum master equation.
result: Chirped-pulse driving can robustly orient the molecule despite cavity coupling, with orientation degree depending on pulse parameters.
conclusion: Chirped-pulse engineering offers a viable route for controlling single-molecule orientation in cavity QED, relevant for hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Fast Collisional $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ Gate For Fermionic Atoms In An Optical Superlattice
authors: Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, And Yoav Sagi

Collisional gates in optical superlattices recently achieved record fidelities, but their operation times are typically limited by tunneling. Here we propose and analyze an alternative route to a fast [MATH] gate for two fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice based on optimized, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063310] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a fast collisional √SWAP gate for fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice using optimized pulse sequences.
motivation: Collisional gates in optical superlattices achieve high fidelities but are slow due to tunneling; a faster gate is needed for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design and optimize a pulse sequence that drives a collisional interaction between two fermionic atoms in a double-well potential, achieving a √SWAP gate via controlled tunneling and on-site interactions.
result: The proposed gate operates significantly faster than conventional tunneling-based gates while maintaining high fidelity, as demonstrated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to fast, high-fidelity two-qubit gates for neutral atom quantum computing platforms.

title: On-demand Single-to-biphoton Conversion In An Atom-coupled Chiral Waveguide
authors: Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. la Rocca, And Jin-Hui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. La Rocca, and Jin-Hui Wu

On-demand generation of photon pairs is here achieved through non-standard waveguide QED, where a four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide. Within such an architecture, resonant four-wave-mixing interactions can be enhanced to the point where an incoming photon, converting into a Stokes and an anti-Stokes photon pair, exhibits generation rates, state purities and cross-correlations that either match or exceed those achieved in most current techniques.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061702] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: On-demand single-to-biphoton conversion via four-wave mixing in a chiral waveguide QED system with a four-level atom.
motivation: Efficient on-demand generation of photon pairs is crucial for quantum networks and information processing; current techniques often suffer from low rates or poor purity.
method: A four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide, enabling resonant four-wave mixing where an incoming photon converts into a Stokes and anti-Stokes photon pair.
result: The scheme achieves generation rates, state purities, and cross-correlations that match or exceed existing techniques.
conclusion: Chiral waveguide QED provides a promising platform for deterministic photon-pair generation, with potential applications in quantum communication and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The MIS problem on unit-disk graphs is NP-hard and can be encoded on Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require many atoms. A more efficient embedding is needed.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to represent arbitrary graphs, leveraging the Rydberg blockade effect to encode the MIS constraint, and analyze the atom count scaling.
result: The 3D embedding reduces the atom overhead compared to 2D embeddings, enabling the encoding of larger graphs with fewer physical qubits.
conclusion: 3D Rydberg atom arrays offer a more resource-efficient platform for solving MIS problems, advancing the practicality of quantum optimization with neutral atoms.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hyperentanglement-based quantum reservoir computing framework that leverages multiple degrees of freedom for enhanced information processing.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is promising but limited by the complexity of implementing nonlinear dynamics; hyperentanglement offers a way to increase computational capacity without additional physical qubits.
method: The authors design a QRC architecture using hyperentangled states (e.g., polarization and orbital angular momentum) as the reservoir, with input encoding and output measurement via linear optics.
result: Numerical simulations show that hyperentanglement-based QRC outperforms standard QRC in tasks like time-series prediction and classification, achieving higher accuracy with fewer resources.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement provides a practical resource for improving QRC performance, bridging quantum information and machine learning.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real experiments suffer from detection loopholes that can compromise the reliability of detection methods.
method: The authors compare the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria under a detection loophole model, analyzing their effectiveness in detecting entanglement with imperfect detectors.
result: They find that the detection loophole significantly reduces the detection capability of both criteria, with the PPT criterion losing its advantage over moment-based criteria in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work highlights the need to account for detection inefficiencies when designing entanglement detection experiments and suggests that moment-based criteria may be more robust in practical scenarios.

title: Direct Observation Of Dynamical Quasicondensation And Generalized Thermalization On Different Quantum Computing Platforms
authors: Philipp Frey And Stephan Rachel

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224306] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization of hard-core bosons on quantum computing platforms.
motivation: To experimentally verify non-equilibrium phenomena predicted for integrable systems, such as dynamical quasicondensation and relaxation to a generalized Gibbs ensemble.
method: The authors simulate hard-core bosons in one dimension using quantum circuits on IBM and Google quantum processors, implementing time evolution and measuring momentum distributions.
result: They directly observe the formation of finite-momentum quasicondensates and confirm that the system thermalizes to a generalized Gibbs ensemble, matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Quantum computers can serve as reliable platforms for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and many-body dynamics, validating theoretical models.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical behavior in the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models, protected by self-duality.
motivation: To understand dynamical phase transitions and multicriticality in stochastic systems, which are relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of kinetically constrained models using large deviation theory and identify lines of self-duality.
result: They demonstrate the existence of dynamical phases separated by self-duality lines and uncover multicritical points where these lines meet.
conclusion: Self-duality provides a mechanism for multicriticality in stochastic dynamics, offering insights into the structure of dynamical phase transitions.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on the information that can be extracted from neural activity via MEG, constrained by metabolic energy and quantum sensing bounds.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit from quantum metrology and the metabolic power available to neural currents to derive an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets a fundamental upper bound on the information capacity of MEG, linking quantum sensing limits to biological energy constraints.
conclusion: The work establishes a quantum thermodynamic bound on a biological measurement technique, highlighting the interplay between information, energy, and quantum limits.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: To understand the interplay between local quantum coherence and global correlations, which is fundamental for quantum resource theories.
method: The authors experimentally prepare quantum states and measure both local coherence and quantum mutual information, observing that their sum is bounded by a fixed upper limit.
result: They find a definitive upper bound on the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information, confirming a local-global trade-off.
conclusion: The results establish a complementarity relation between local and global quantum resources, with implications for quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across different stochastic regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in systems with discrete state transitions, relevant to information thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates, via phase transitions, can process high-dimensional environmental information, linking phase separation to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex signals to respond to their environment; the authors explore whether phase transitions in biomolecular condensates offer a physical mechanism for such information processing.
method: The paper is a perspective that synthesizes concepts from phase transitions, information theory, and cellular biology, proposing a framework where condensates act as computational elements.
result: It suggests that phase separation can implement classification, sensing, and decision-making, potentially enabling efficient processing of high-dimensional inputs.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a plausible and powerful paradigm for cellular information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental investigation.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite in many-body chaotic systems, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the absence of a sharp Trotterization transition, impacting the design of quantum simulations.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that uses a tight-binding lattice to represent ancillary degrees of freedom, combined with moment-matching to achieve near-optimal query complexity.
result: The framework yields quantum algorithms with near-optimal scaling for solving linear differential equations, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum information processing and simulation.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise correlations in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle at intermediate frequencies.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique fills a gap in qubit noise characterization, offering a practical tool for improving qubit coherence and understanding decoherence mechanisms.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction are still developing.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated, enabling megaquop-scale computations with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The transversal architecture makes neutral-atom quantum simulators more practical for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation, advancing the feasibility of quantum advantage in this platform.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under noise, relating it to the expressivity of the circuit measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra. They use techniques from random matrix theory and quantum information theory.
result: They show that noise can reduce the concentration of the loss function, making gradients more accessible, and that circuits with lower expressivity are more resilient to noise-induced concentration.
conclusion: The findings provide a principled roadmap for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training, bridging quantum information theory and practical quantum machine learning.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulations and non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to explore string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics, not just simple breaking.
conclusion: The findings provide new probes for studying confinement and non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in analog quantum simulators.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme allows parallel measurements without requiring additional code blocks, improving computational efficiency.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel logical operations on LDPC codes.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally demonstrate suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple, effective method for leakage protection in exchange-only spin qubits, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: This work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework and comparative analysis will help researchers navigate and apply non-Markovian simulation methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce circuit complexity and resource requirements for certain gates and algorithms.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can reduce the number of operations, though practical challenges remain.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, but further development in control and error correction is needed.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: Analyzes optimal probe states and measurement strategies for multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries, achieving Heisenberg scaling in certain settings.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is crucial for quantum metrology, and understanding resource requirements for simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is a key challenge.
method: The authors consider two-bosonic-mode scenarios, identify optimal probe states in fixed-particle-number subspaces, and analyze precision scaling using expectation values of generators and their moments.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and analogous states for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters; with restricted measurements, twin-Fock states enable Heisenberg scaling for two parameters.
conclusion: The work extends single-parameter intuition to multiparameter settings, highlighting the role of specific entangled states and measurement restrictions in achieving optimal precision.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-inefficient without using symmetry information.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: On The Dynamical Lie Algebras Of Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms
authors: Jonathan Allcock, Miklos Santha, Pei Yuan, And Shengyu Zhang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2119 (2026).

Dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) have emerged as a valuable tool in the study of parameterized quantum circuits, helping to characterize both their expressiveness and trainability. In particular, the absence or presence of barren plateaus (BPs) – flat regions in parameter space that prevent the efficient training of variational quantum algorithms – has recently been shown to be intimately related to quantities derived from the associated DLA. In this work, we investigate DLAs for the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), one of the most studied variational quantum algorithms for solving graph MaxCut and other combinatorial optimization problems. While DLAs for QAOA circuits have been studied before, existing results have either been based on numerical evidence, or else correspond to DLA generators specifically chosen to be universal for quantum computation on a subspace of states. We initiate an analytical study of barren plateaus and other statistics of QAOA algorithms, and give bounds on the dimensions of the corresponding DLAs and their centers for general graphs. We then focus on the [MATH]-vertex cycle and complete graphs. For the cycle graph we give an explicit basis, identify its decomposition into the direct sum of a [MATH]-dimensional center and a semisimple component isomorphic to [MATH] copies of [MATH]. We give an explicit basis for this isomorphism, and a closed-form expression for the variance of the cost function, proving the absence of BPs. For the complete graph we prove that the dimension of the DLA is [MATH] and give an explicit basis for the DLA.

.
tldr: This paper analytically studies dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) for QAOA circuits, providing bounds on DLA dimensions and proving absence of barren plateaus for cycle graphs.
motivation: Understanding the trainability and expressiveness of variational quantum algorithms like QAOA is crucial for their practical use; barren plateaus hinder training, and DLA analysis offers a way to characterize them.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on DLA dimensions and centers for general graphs, then explicitly compute DLAs for cycle and complete graphs using representation theory and Lie algebra decompositions.
result: For cycle graphs, the DLA decomposes into a center and a semisimple part isomorphic to copies of sl(2), and the cost function variance is computed, proving no barren plateaus. For complete graphs, the DLA dimension is n^2-1 with an explicit basis.
conclusion: The work provides rigorous analytical results on QAOA DLAs, confirming the absence of barren plateaus for certain graphs and offering tools for further study of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Tensor Cross Interpolation Of Purities In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Dmytro Kolisnyk, Raimel A. Medina, Romain Vasseur, And Maksym Serbyn
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2114 (2026).

A defining feature of quantum many-body systems is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space with the number of degrees of freedom. This exponential complexity naïvely renders a complete state characterization, for instance via the complete set of bipartite Renyi entropies for all disjoint regions, a challenging task. Recently, a compact way of storing subregions' purities by encoding them as amplitudes of a fictitious quantum wave function, known as entanglement feature, was proposed. Notably, the entanglement feature can be a simple object even for highly entangled quantum states. However the complexity and practical usage of the entanglement feature for general quantum states has not been explored. In this work, we demonstrate that the entanglement feature can be efficiently learned using only a polynomial amount of samples in the number of degrees of freedom through the so-called tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm, assuming it is expressible as a finite bond dimension MPS. We benchmark this learning process on Haar and random MPS states, confirming analytic expectations. Applying the TCI algorithm to quantum eigenstates of various one dimensional quantum systems, we identify cases where eigenstates have entanglement feature learnable with TCI. We conclude with possible applications of the learned entanglement feature, such as quantifying the distance between different entanglement patterns and finding the optimal one-dimensional ordering of physical indices in a given state, highlighting the potential utility of the proposed purity interpolation method.

.
tldr: This paper uses tensor cross interpolation to efficiently learn the entanglement feature (set of bipartite Rényi entropies) of quantum many-body states, demonstrating polynomial scaling in system size.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in many-body systems is exponentially hard; the entanglement feature offers a compact representation, but its practical extraction was unexplored.
method: The authors apply the tensor cross interpolation (TCI) algorithm to learn the entanglement feature as a matrix product state (MPS) from a polynomial number of samples, assuming the feature is expressible as a finite-bond-dimension MPS.
result: TCI successfully learns entanglement features for Haar random states, random MPS, and certain eigenstates of 1D quantum systems, with sample complexity scaling polynomially in system size.
conclusion: The learned entanglement feature enables quantifying distances between entanglement patterns and finding optimal 1D orderings, highlighting its utility for many-body entanglement analysis.

title: From Spin Squeezing To Fast State Discrimination
authors: Michael R. Geller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2108 (2026).

There is great interest in generating and controlling entanglement in Bose-Einstein condensates and similar ensembles for use in quantum computation, simulation, and sensing. One class of entangled states useful for enhanced metrology are spin-squeezed states of [MATH] two-level atoms. After preparing a spin coherent state of width [MATH] centered at coordinates [MATH] on the Bloch sphere, atomic interactions generate a nonlinear evolution that shears the state's probability density, stretching it to an ellipse and causing squeezing in a direction perpendicular to the major axis. Here we consider the same setup but in the [MATH] limit . This shrinks the initial coherent state to zero area. Large [MATH] also suppresses two-particle entanglement and squeezing, as required by a monogamy bound. The torsion (1-axis twist) is still present, however, and the center of the large [MATH] coherent state evolves as a qubit governed by a two-state Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The resulting nonlinearity is known to be a powerful resource in quantum computation. It can be used to implement single-input quantum state discrimination, an impossibility within linear one-particle quantum mechanics. We obtain a solution to the discrimination problem in terms of a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. We also consider an open-system variant containing both Bloch sphere torsion and dissipation. In this case it should be possible to generate two basins of attraction within the Bloch ball, having a shared boundary that can be used for a type of autonomous state discrimination. We explore these and other connections between spin squeezing in the large [MATH] limit and nonlinear quantum gates, and argue that a two-component condensate is a promising platform for realizing a nonlinear qubit.

.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between spin squeezing in the large-N limit and nonlinear quantum gates for state discrimination.
motivation: To understand how spin squeezing in Bose-Einstein condensates can be used for quantum computation and sensing, particularly in the large-N limit where entanglement is suppressed but nonlinearity remains.
method: The author analyzes the evolution of a spin coherent state under one-axis twisting in the large-N limit, deriving a nonlinear qubit dynamics governed by a Gross-Pitaevskii equation, and considers both closed and open systems.
result: The nonlinearity enables single-input quantum state discrimination, with a solution given by a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere; in the open-system case, two basins of attraction emerge for autonomous discrimination.
conclusion: Two-component Bose-Einstein condensates are a promising platform for realizing nonlinear qubits with applications in quantum state discrimination.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator localization and fragmentation in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and an entanglement bottleneck.
motivation: Understanding the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and ergodicity.
method: The authors construct a nearest-neighbor Floquet-Clifford circuit with brickwork pattern and introduce disordered non-Clifford perturbations. They analyze operator spreading, fragmentation, and spectral form factor analytically and numerically.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors with emergent local integrals of motion. The average operator spreading length is tunable, and initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across fragment boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, with implications for thermalization and quantum chaos in driven systems.

title: Phase-Sensitive Measurements On A Fermi–Hubbard Quantum Processor
authors: Alberto R. Cavallar, Luis Escalera-Moreno, Titus Franz, Timon Hilker, J. Ignacio Cirac, Philipp M. Preiss, And Benjamin F. Schiffer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2103 (2026).

Fermionic quantum processors are a promising platform for quantum simulation of correlated fermionic matter. In this work, we study a hardware-efficient protocol for measuring complex expectation values of the time-evolution operator, commonly referred to as Loschmidt echoes, with fermions in an optical superlattice. We analyze the algorithm for the Fermi–Hubbard model at half-filling as well as at finite doping. The method relies on global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution, the latter being realized by architecture-tailored pulse sequences starting from a product state of plaquettes. Our numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range. This allows one to measure spectral properties of the Fermi–Hubbard model, such as the local density of states, and paves the way for the study of finite-temperature properties in current fermionic quantum simulators.

.
tldr: Proposes a hardware-efficient protocol for measuring Loschmidt echoes on a fermionic quantum processor to study spectral properties of the Fermi-Hubbard model.
motivation: Fermionic quantum processors are promising for simulating correlated fermionic matter, but measuring complex expectation values like Loschmidt echoes efficiently remains challenging.
method: The protocol uses global quench dynamics and short imaginary time evolution realized by architecture-tailored pulse sequences starting from a product state of plaquettes.
result: Numerical results show that complex Loschmidt echoes can be efficiently obtained for large many-body states over a broad spectral range.
conclusion: This enables measurement of spectral properties such as local density of states and paves the way for studying finite-temperature properties in current fermionic quantum simulators.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs over 21 km fiber.
motivation: Asymmetric HOM revival interference in QFCs had not been systematically investigated, and efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals was unreported.
method: Experimental setup with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, HOM interference measurements across multiple time-bins, and distribution over 21 km optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: Observed HOM revivals up to 20 time-bins with visibilities around 70%, and distributed QFC over 21 km fiber with 12 time-bin photon bunching and 70.5% visibility.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Absolutely Maximally Entangled Pure States Of Multipartite Quantum Systems
authors: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Rafał Bistroń, Albert Rico, Arul Lakshminarayan And Karol Życzkowski
abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states of a system composed of N parties are distinguished by the property that for any splitting at least one partial trace is maximally mixed. Due to maximal possible correlations between any two selected subsystems these states have numerous applications in various fields of quantum information processing including multi-user teleportation, quantum error correction and secret sharing. We present an updated survey of various techniques to generate such strongly entangled states, including those going beyond the standard construction of graph and stabilizer states. Our contribution includes, in particular, analysis of the degree of entanglement of reduced states obtained by partial trace of AME projectors, states obtained by a symmetric superposition of GHZ states, an orthogonal frequency square representation of the ‘golden’ AME state and an updated summary of the number of local unitary equivalence classes.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of absolutely maximally entangled (AME) pure states, their constructions, and applications in quantum information.
motivation: AME states are crucial for multipartite quantum protocols like teleportation, error correction, and secret sharing, but their classification and construction remain challenging.
method: The authors review known techniques (graph states, stabilizer states, symmetric GHZ superpositions, orthogonal frequency squares) and present new results on entanglement of reduced states and local unitary equivalence classes.
result: They provide an updated classification of AME states, including new constructions and an analysis of the number of local unitary equivalence classes for small N and local dimensions.
conclusion: AME states are a rich resource for quantum information, and the survey clarifies their structure and generation methods, aiding future applications.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to make non-Markovian master equations more tractable by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals.
motivation: Simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains accuracy while reducing complexity.
method: They express the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the use of an extended Markovian master equation with auxiliary degrees of freedom.
result: The approximation yields accurate dynamics for a range of non-Markovian regimes, significantly lowering computational cost compared to exact methods.
conclusion: This approach makes non-Markovian simulations more accessible, facilitating studies of open quantum systems in quantum thermodynamics and related fields.

title: Geometric Algebra Quantum Gate Decomposition
authors: Zeno Toffano Youssef Amraoui
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum gates are usually described through matrix and tensor-product formalisms that often obscure their geometric structure. In this work, we formulate the Pauli and Clifford groups within the complex Geometric Algebra (GA) framework. We show that the Pauli group is naturally identified with the group of blades up to a global phase, thereby providing a geometric interpretation of Pauli operators and their commutation relations in terms of oriented subspaces. We further prove that Clifford operators are generated by products of {\pi}/4-Pauli rotors and introduce a greedy Pauli rotor decomposition algorithm whose empirical behavior suggests unexpectedly compact decompositions for Clifford operators. Finally, we show that Clifford+T universality admits a natural geometric interpretation through {\pi}/8-rotors within this framework.
tldr: This paper reformulates Pauli and Clifford groups using geometric algebra, providing a geometric interpretation of quantum gates and a greedy decomposition algorithm.
motivation: Standard matrix and tensor-product formalisms obscure the geometric structure of quantum gates; a geometric algebra framework may offer new insights and more efficient decompositions.
method: The authors identify Pauli operators with blades in complex geometric algebra, show Clifford operators are generated by π/4-Pauli rotors, and propose a greedy rotor decomposition algorithm.
result: The Pauli group is naturally identified with blade groups up to phase, Clifford operators admit compact decompositions via the greedy algorithm, and Clifford+T universality is interpreted through π/8-rotors.
conclusion: Geometric algebra provides a unified geometric language for quantum gate decomposition, potentially simplifying circuit synthesis and offering new perspectives on quantum computation.

title: Influence-solvability: A Systematic Theory Of $(1+1)d$ Solvability And Its Application To Brickwork Circuits
authors: Sun Woo P. Kim Friedrich H\"ubner
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: `Solvable' circuits, such as dual unitaries and its generalisations, have arisen as paradigmatic examples of tractable chaotic non-equilibrium dynamics, both in classical and quantum systems. However, while increasingly more complicated sufficient conditions have been proposed, a systematic theory classifying and understanding general features of solvable circuits is missing. We develop such a theory by introducing influence-solvable circuits, a class of [MATH] circuits whose influence matrix, which represents the `bath' generated by its own evolution, is given by a uniform MPS with finite bond-dimension [MATH]. This property allows for efficient computation of subsystem dynamics and essentially contains all known examples of solvable circuits. We derive a set of necessary and sufficient local conditions by using a version of the fundamental theorem of MPS for open boundary conditions. Next we apply our theory to brickwork circuits with [MATH] influence-solvability and perform a systematic classification of classical brickwork circuits with local dimension up to [MATH] and quantum brickwork circuits with [MATH]. Our search reveals new solvable circuits that are not captured by known solvability conditions.
tldr: Introduces influence-solvable circuits, a class of 1+1D circuits whose influence matrix is a uniform MPS, enabling efficient computation of subsystem dynamics and classification of solvable circuits.
motivation: Existing solvable circuits like dual unitaries lack a systematic theory; the authors aim to develop a unified framework to classify and understand all solvable circuits.
method: They define influence-solvability via the influence matrix being a uniform MPS with finite bond dimension, derive necessary and sufficient local conditions using the fundamental theorem of MPS, and perform a systematic classification of brickwork circuits.
result: The classification reveals new solvable circuits not captured by known conditions, and the framework unifies all known examples of solvable circuits.
conclusion: Influence-solvability provides a systematic theory for solvable circuits, enabling efficient computation and discovery of new solvable models.

This property enables efficient computation of subsystem dynamics and encompasses all previously known solvable circuits, such as dual-unitary circuits and their generalizations. The authors derive necessary and sufficient local conditions for influence-solvability using a version of the fundamental theorem of MPS for open boundary conditions. They then apply this theory to brickwork circuits, performing a systematic classification for classical circuits with local dimension d up to 3 and quantum circuits with d=2. The classification reveals new solvable circuits that were not captured by earlier solvability conditions, demonstrating the power of the influence-solvability framework.
