Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems using imaginary time spectral transforms and tensor networks.
motivation: Preparing excited states is important for understanding quantum systems, but existing methods are often computationally expensive or require matrix inversion.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion, implemented via tensor-network simulations.
result: Demonstrated on disordered spin chains, showing effective preparation of excited eigenstates.
conclusion: The method provides a scalable approach for excited-state preparation, compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts
abstract:
Author(s): Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, and Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic methods for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS) for lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative physics but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods like PEPS offer an alternative, but require handling gauge redundancy and symmetries.
method: The authors introduce a gauge fixing procedure for Gaussian fermionic PEPS and develop algorithms to impose translation invariance, enabling efficient simulation of gauge theories in the thermodynamic limit.
result: They demonstrate the methods on a 2D Z2 gauge theory, showing that gauge fixing and translation invariance lead to accurate ground state energies and reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed algorithmic framework makes gauged Gaussian fermionic PEPS a practical tool for studying lattice gauge theories, particularly in regimes where Monte Carlo methods fail.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, driven by topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems beyond conventional superconductivity.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches for quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton superfluidity with unique properties.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a robust platform for engineering anyonic superfluids.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging conventional assumptions.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum spin and dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific geometries, analyzing ground state properties and phase separation.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, leading to a breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation challenges traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit in quantum many-body systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified framework.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable dynamics and the relationship with quantum computation.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding and solving quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuits.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, including their formation and quantum features.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmions, covering their topological field configurations and quantum interactions.
result: Summarizes current understanding of skyrmion quantum properties and their potential for spintronic applications.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Squeezing Enhancement In Lossy Multi-Path Atom Interferometers
authors: Julian Günther, Jan-Niclas Kirsten-Siemß, Naceur Gaaloul, And Klemens Hammerer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2122 (2026).

This paper explores the sensitivity gains afforded by spin-squeezed states in atom interferometry, in particular using Bragg diffraction. We introduce a generalised input-output formalism that accurately describes realistic, non-unitary interferometers, including losses due to velocity selectivity and scattering into undesired momentum states. This formalism is applied to evaluate the performance of one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states in improving phase sensitivity. Our results show that by carefully optimising the parameters of the Bragg beam splitters and controlling the degree of squeezing, it is possible to improve the sensitivity of the interferometer by several dB with respect to the standard quantum limit despite realistic levels of losses in light pulse operations. However, the analysis also highlights the challenges associated with achieving these improvements in practice, most notably the impact of finite temperature on the benefits of entanglement. The results suggest ways of optimising interferometric setups to exploit quantum entanglement under realistic conditions, thereby contributing to advances in precision metrology with atom interferometers.

.
tldr: This paper studies sensitivity enhancement in lossy atom interferometers using spin-squeezed states, focusing on practical metrology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Atom interferometers are limited by the standard quantum limit; spin squeezing can improve sensitivity but is degraded by losses and temperature.
method: A generalized input-output formalism is developed to model non-unitary interferometers with losses, and one-axis twisted spin-squeezed states are evaluated.
result: Optimizing Bragg beam splitter parameters and squeezing can yield several dB improvement over the standard quantum limit despite realistic losses.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can enhance atom interferometry under realistic conditions, but finite temperature poses a significant challenge.

title: Optimizing Qubo On A Quantum Computer By Mimicking Imaginary Time Evolution
authors: Yahui Chai And Alice Di Tucci
abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum–classical algorithm for solving quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems using an imaginary time evolution-mimicking circuit (ITEMC). The circuit parameters are optimized to mimic short-time ITE, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values. This significantly reduces the measurement overhead by avoiding full energy evaluation. By updating the initial state based on results from last step iteratively, the algorithm quickly converges to the low-energy solutions. With a pre-sorting step that optimizes quantum gate ordering based on QUBO coefficients, the convergence is further improved. Our classical simulations achieve approximation ratios above up to 150 qubits. Furthermore, the linear scaling of entanglement entropy with system size suggests that the circuit is challenging to simulate classically using tensor networks. We also demonstrate hardware runs on IBM’s device for 40, 60, and 80 qubits, and obtain solutions compatible with that from simulated annealing.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for solving QUBO problems using a circuit that mimics imaginary time evolution.
motivation: QUBO problems are important for combinatorial optimization, but current quantum algorithms require many measurements or deep circuits.
method: The algorithm optimizes a parameterized quantum circuit to approximate short-time imaginary time evolution, using only single- and two-qubit expectation values to avoid full energy evaluation, and iteratively updates the initial state.
result: Classical simulations achieve high approximation ratios for up to 150 qubits, and hardware runs on IBM devices for up to 80 qubits yield solutions comparable to simulated annealing.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm reduces measurement overhead and converges quickly, but its primary contribution is to combinatorial optimization rather than the user's core research directions.

title: Percolation With Coupled Lasers: Effect Of Non-linearities On The Phase Transition
authors: Simon Mahler, Nikita Stroev, Mahmoud Abu Rmilah, Asher Friesem And Nir Davidson
abstract: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging due to difficulties in tuning site connectivity, isolating local interactions, and mitigating finite-size effects. In this work, we experimentally investigate percolation with a platform of coupled lasers, where connectivity, interaction strength, and system size can be controlled. Using a square array of lasers with astronomical number of possible cluster configurations, we show that the emergence of a percolating cluster corresponds to the onset of phase locking among the lasers. We also show that the percolation probability undergoes a second-order alike transition as a function of the site-occupation probability, with a threshold consistent with classical theoretical predictions. Surprisingly, we find that at low pump level, amplified mode competition (nonlinear regime) alters the effective behavior of the lasing sites and modify the nature of the percolation transition. The experimental results are interpreted by the means of a theoretical toy model with connectivity rules to the classical percolation.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies percolation using a coupled laser array, showing that the percolation transition corresponds to phase locking and that nonlinearities modify the transition.
motivation: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging; the authors use a coupled laser platform to overcome difficulties in tuning connectivity and isolating interactions.
method: A square array of coupled lasers with controllable site-occupation probability is used to observe percolation; experimental results are compared to a theoretical toy model with connectivity rules.
result: The percolation probability undergoes a second-order-like transition with threshold consistent with classical predictions, but low pump level nonlinearities alter the effective behavior and modify the transition.
conclusion: The coupled laser platform enables controlled percolation studies, and nonlinear effects can change the nature of the phase transition.

title: Hybrid Monte Carlo For Fractional Quantum Hall States
authors: Ting-Tung Wang, Ha Quang Trung, Qianhui Xu, Min Long, Bo Yang And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: We develop a hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) method to efficiently compute the physical observables from the samplings of the Laughlin and the Moore–Read (MR) wave functions of fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems. With the advancements in methodology, including global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry, our HMC simulation is significantly faster than the widely used Metropolis Monte Carlo scheme. As a result, we can readily simulate systems with electron numbers on both disk and sphere geometries. We apply this method to investigate the topological shift obtained from the edge dipole moment, computed from the wave function density on the disk. We also numerically computed the non-Abelian braiding matrices for different braiding schemes of the MR quasiholes on the sphere. Results with much better quality compared with previous works have been achieved. With the thermodynamic limit results obtained at ease, we also discuss the future usage of our method to clarify the questions on the instability of FQH states in an ideal Chern band setting or under quantum decoherence.
tldr: Develops a hybrid Monte Carlo method for simulating fractional quantum Hall wave functions, focusing on computational efficiency and topological properties.
motivation: Efficiently compute observables from Laughlin and Moore-Read wave functions for large systems, overcoming limitations of standard Metropolis Monte Carlo.
method: Uses hybrid Monte Carlo with global updates and double stereographic projection on spherical geometry to sample FQH wave functions.
result: Achieves significantly faster simulations, enabling computation of topological shift and non-Abelian braiding matrices with improved quality.
conclusion: The method facilitates thermodynamic limit studies and can address questions on FQH state stability in Chern bands or under decoherence.

title: Effective Geometry And Position-Dependent Mass In Dual-$q$ Quantum Mechanics
authors: A. Makhlouf A. Boumali
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the deformed-derivative formalism introduced by Borges, with emphasis on the relation between the linear operator [MATH] and its nonlinear dual counterpart [MATH]. Directly inserting the dual derivative into the kinetic term leads to a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation and obscures the usual interpretation of superposition and probability. We show that this nonlinearity can be removed by a simultaneous transformation of the coordinate and of the wave function. The transformed problem is an ordinary linear Schr\"odinger equation in a deformed coordinate, and its representation in the physical coordinate is equivalent to a Hermitian position-dependent-mass (PDM) Hamiltonian. In this formulation, the deformation parameter [MATH] determines both the effective mass profile and the associated metric. The formalism is applied to the free particle, the infinite square well, the rectangular barrier, and the harmonic oscillator in the weak-deformation regime. Comparison with the nonadditive-translation approach of Costa Filho shows that the Borges dual-[MATH] framework provides an alternative route to the same effective geometric structure. For [MATH], the effective confinement length is reduced, which raises the bound-state spectrum and enhances tunneling; for [MATH], the effective length is increased, which lowers the spectrum and suppresses tunneling relative to the undeformed limit [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies a deformed-derivative formalism leading to a position-dependent-mass Hamiltonian, applied to simple quantum systems.
motivation: To resolve nonlinearity in a dual-q deformed Schrödinger equation by transforming to an effective linear equation with a deformed coordinate.
method: The authors apply a simultaneous coordinate and wavefunction transformation to convert the nonlinear equation into a linear one with a position-dependent mass, then solve for free particle, infinite well, barrier, and harmonic oscillator in the weak-deformation regime.
result: The deformation parameter modifies the effective confinement length, raising or lowering bound-state spectra and enhancing or suppressing tunneling compared to the undeformed case.
conclusion: The Borges dual-q framework provides an alternative geometric interpretation equivalent to a position-dependent mass Hamiltonian, but the work is primarily a mathematical extension without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quasi-Product States And Factor Types For The One-Dimensional Hard-Core Model
authors: Yuri Suhov Farrukh Mukhamedov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a quasi-product state associated with the one-dimensional hard-core Gibbs measure. After coding the model by the topological Markov chain, we construct the standard path [MATH]-algebra of admissible hard-core words and show that the stationary Markov measure induces on it a faithful diagonal state in the sense of Evans. We then analyze the von Neumann algebra generated by the corresponding GNS representation. The resulting algebra is a hyperfinite factor, and its type is determined by the single parameter \(\kappa=q/p^2,\) where \(p&q\\ 1&0\) is the transition matrix of the Markov chain. More precisely, the factor is of type [MATH] when [MATH], and of type [MATH] with \( \l=\min\{\kappa,\kappa^{-1}\}\) for [MATH]. We also specify the centralizer and the weight flow for the resulting factor.
tldr: This paper studies quasi-product states and von Neumann algebra factors for the one-dimensional hard-core Gibbs measure, using topological Markov chains and GNS representations.
motivation: To understand the structure of quasi-product states arising from hard-core interactions and classify the resulting von Neumann algebras.
method: The hard-core model is coded by a topological Markov chain, a path C*-algebra of admissible words is constructed, and the GNS representation of the stationary Markov state is analyzed.
result: The von Neumann algebra is a hyperfinite factor whose type depends on the parameter κ = q/p^2: type III_λ when κ≠1 and type II_1 when κ=1.
conclusion: The work provides a complete classification of the factor type for this class of states, linking statistical mechanics to operator algebras.

title: The Formation Of Magnetic Reentrancy In The Ising Model On A Decorated Square Lattice
authors: F. A. Kassan-Ogly A. V. Zarubin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our work, based on an exact solution of the Ising model on a decorated square lattice with an arbitrary number of decorating spins, we have demonstrated the fundamental possibility of describing the phenomenon of multiple magnetic phase transitions (magnetic reentrancy) in the regime of competing exchange interactions. We analyzed the magnetic behavior of the system and established the conditions for the occurrence of magnetic reentrancy. We have determined the relationships of the model parameter under which the formation of one, three, and even five magnetic phase transitions is possible, which is confirmed by a complicated magnetic phase diagram. We have also proposed a unique method for finding critical temperatures that allows for the precise determination of their number and values, including those at extremely low temperatures.
tldr: This paper exactly solves the Ising model on a decorated square lattice to demonstrate multiple magnetic phase transitions (magnetic reentrancy) under competing interactions.
motivation: To understand the fundamental possibility of multiple magnetic phase transitions in a simple statistical mechanical model.
method: Exact solution of the Ising model on a decorated square lattice with arbitrary number of decorating spins, using transfer matrix or related techniques.
result: Conditions for one, three, or five magnetic phase transitions are established, and a method for precisely determining critical temperatures is proposed.
conclusion: Magnetic reentrancy can be described within the exactly solvable Ising model, providing a theoretical framework for multiple phase transitions.

title: Discrete Phase Symmetry Of Stationary States In Bichromatically Pumped Kerr Microresonators
authors: Boulat Nougmanov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bichromatically pumped Kerr microresonators exhibit phase bistability and multistability arising from four-wave mixing between pump and generated modes. Here we analyze the symmetry structure of stationary solutions in the coupled-mode description of such systems. We show that the two-pump coupled-mode equations are a particular case of a more general model with pumps placed at equally spaced modes. For this model, any stationary solution generates a finite family of stationary solutions through a discrete phase transformation. This transformation leaves the equations invariant and preserves the stability type of the corresponding stationary states. As a consequence, the possible stationary values of each individual mode form a regular polygon in the complex plane. The number of vertices is determined by the order of the mode index [MATH] in the group [MATH], where [MATH] is the separation between the pumped modes. Thus, the phase multistability structure depends not only on nonlinear dynamics but also on the arithmetic relation between the mode index and the pump separation. These results provide a simple symmetry-based explanation for the discrete phase structure observed in multimode Kerr resonators under bichromatic pumping.
tldr: This paper analyzes discrete phase symmetry in stationary states of bichromatically pumped Kerr microresonators, revealing a regular polygon structure in mode phases determined by arithmetic relations.
motivation: Understanding the symmetry and multistability structure in Kerr microresonators under bichromatic pumping is important for nonlinear optics and frequency comb generation.
method: The authors derive a general coupled-mode model for pumps at equally spaced modes and identify a discrete phase transformation that leaves the equations invariant, preserving stability.
result: Stationary solutions form families related by discrete phase rotations; the number of vertices in the phase polygon is determined by the mode index modulo the pump separation.
conclusion: The phase multistability in such systems is governed by a simple symmetry principle rooted in arithmetic relations, providing a unified explanation for observed discrete phase structures.

title: Explicit Quantum Circuit Simulation Of Nonlinear 1-Dimensional Fluid With Carleman-linearized Boltzmann Method
authors: Keita Kanno, Kazumasa Ueno, Hayato Higuchi, Morimasa Okamoto, Yuya Yoshizuru, Ryoya Ishimaru, Towa Takagi, Kentaro Sakamoto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computation of fluid dynamics has attracted growing attention as a key application of fault-tolerant quantum computers anticipated in the coming decade, with lattice Boltzmann methods emerging as a particularly promising approach. Explicit and efficient elementary-gate-level circuit simulations, however, have so far been demonstrated only in the linear case. Here we include the leading nonlinearity through second-order Carleman linearization of the one-dimensional Boltzmann equation, and demonstrate, via explicit quantum-circuit simulation, the preparation of the final-time state using a Taylor-expansion-based ODE solver based on the quantum singular value transformation. With this construction, we analyze the gate and qubit complexities, which scale logarithmically with the grid size, the nonlinearity captured by the higher-order Carleman linearization, and the practical utility of higher-order expansions in the Taylor ODE solver. The construction provides a concrete baseline for computational cost reduction and further developments such as extensions to higher dimensions, complex geometries, and the extraction of physical quantities, towards industrially useful quantum CFD.
tldr: This paper simulates nonlinear 1D fluid dynamics on a quantum computer using Carleman linearization and quantum singular value transformation.
motivation: Quantum simulation of fluid dynamics is a promising application for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but explicit circuit-level simulations have been limited to linear cases.
method: The authors apply second-order Carleman linearization to the 1D Boltzmann equation and use a Taylor-expansion-based ODE solver via quantum singular value transformation to prepare the final-time state.
result: Gate and qubit complexities scale logarithmically with grid size; the approach captures nonlinearity and demonstrates explicit quantum circuit simulation.
conclusion: This work provides a baseline for quantum computational fluid dynamics, with potential extensions to higher dimensions and complex geometries.

title: Beyond-Third-Order Quantum Coherence In Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy Via Order-Selective Isolation
authors: Xue Zhang, De-Ran Zhang, Hui Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in nonlinear spectroscopy is the order-selective readout of weak higher-order responses that spectrally overlap with dominant lower-order signals. This bottleneck is particularly severe in two-dimensional (2D) spectroscopy, where extending conventional phase-cycling schemes to higher orders rapidly increases measurement and analysis complexity. Here we introduce a computation-assisted strategy that combines rotating-frame acquisition with a frame-shift tracking algorithm to separate signals by their frame-dependent spectral shifts. In a rubidium vapor experiment, we use this approach to isolate a 7th-order nonlinear contribution from coexisting 3rd-order components, enabling direct access to higher-order quantum-coherence dynamics without sacrificing operation at comparatively high pulse intensities. The method is broadly compatible with multidimensional spectroscopy platforms and provides a practical route to probing many-body and collective ultrafast dynamics beyond third order.
tldr: A computation-assisted method to isolate higher-order quantum coherence signals in 2D spectroscopy.
motivation: Higher-order nonlinear signals in 2D spectroscopy are weak and overlap with dominant lower-order signals, making them difficult to measure.
method: Combines rotating-frame acquisition with a frame-shift tracking algorithm to separate signals by frame-dependent spectral shifts.
result: Successfully isolated a 7th-order nonlinear contribution from coexisting 3rd-order components in a rubidium vapor experiment.
conclusion: The method enables direct access to higher-order quantum-coherence dynamics without sacrificing pulse intensity, and is broadly compatible with multidimensional spectroscopy platforms.

title: Quantum Walk-based Optimisation For Capacitated Vehicle Routing With Homogeneous And Heterogeneous Fleets
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Aidan Smith, Callum Neill, Paulo Santos, Ugo Varetto, Jingbo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) is an appealing candidate for quantum optimisation due to its combinatorial complexity and practical importance. However, the problem's constrained search space poses a challenge for such quantum algorithms. We introduce a quantum walk-based optimisation algorithm (QWOA) for the CVRP with homogeneous or heterogeneous vehicle fleets, addressing this challenge through a continuous-time quantum walk over a product space that coincides with combinatorial structures intrinsic to the CVRP solution space. Relative to the prior QWOA-based formulation, this approach reduces the per-layer gate complexity from [MATH] to [MATH] and supports a circuit parameterisation schedule generated by a fixed number of classical parameters. Exact state-vector simulation on instances with up to [MATH] customers and [MATH] vehicles demonstrates improved convergence to low-cost solutions using markedly fewer objective function evaluations, with the advantage broadening as problem size increases. These results identify structured product-space walks as a promising tool for optimisation over constrained combinatorial spaces.
tldr: This paper applies a quantum walk-based optimization algorithm to the capacitated vehicle routing problem, a classical combinatorial optimization problem.
motivation: The capacitated vehicle routing problem is combinatorially complex and practically important, making it a candidate for quantum optimization.
method: The authors introduce a continuous-time quantum walk over a product space that matches the combinatorial structure of the CVRP, reducing gate complexity and using a fixed number of classical parameters.
result: Exact state-vector simulations on instances with up to 12 customers and 4 vehicles show improved convergence to low-cost solutions with fewer objective function evaluations compared to prior QWOA formulations.
conclusion: Structured product-space quantum walks are a promising tool for optimization over constrained combinatorial spaces.

title: Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Induced By Spatial Noncommutativity
authors: Su-Peng Kou Zheng Wei
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In all known schemes for the non-Hermitian skin effect, the non-Hermitian ingredient that drives the skin localization, whether asymmetric hopping or gain and loss, is invariably introduced by hand as an independent model parameter along the skin direction. Here we show that when two spatial coordinates do not commute, the skin effect can break free of this paradigm: a gain-loss potential applied along one coordinate automatically generates non-reciprocity along the other through the coordinate noncommutativity, driving all eigenstates to pile up exponentially at a boundary. We term this phenomenon the noncommutative skin effect. The inverse skin length is proportional to the noncommutativity parameter and is given by an analytic formula, exact in the thermodynamic limit and verified by exact diagonalization of lattice models; the reflection symmetry of the imaginary potential furnishes an exact criterion for the presence or absence of the effect, valid rigorously for finite-size systems. For a sinusoidal imaginary potential, the skin direction of all eigenstates flips collectively at parameter points fixed purely by geometry. Because the flip point is independent of the potential strength, the reversal constitutes a zero-crossing measurement scheme intrinsically robust against systematic errors, from which the noncommutativity parameter can be extracted directly. The qualitative transition of the eigenstates from uniform to exponentially localized renders the effect a nonperturbative probe of spatial noncommutativity, and the Peierls-phase structure of its lattice model is in principle accessible to cold-atom synthetic dimensions, photonic resonators, and topolectrical circuits.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-Hermitian skin effect driven by spatial noncommutativity, where a gain-loss potential along one coordinate induces non-reciprocity along another.
motivation: To find a new mechanism for the non-Hermitian skin effect that does not require manually introducing non-Hermitian terms along the skin direction.
method: The authors use analytic formulas in the thermodynamic limit and exact diagonalization of lattice models to demonstrate the effect, and propose a zero-crossing measurement scheme.
result: The inverse skin length is proportional to the noncommutativity parameter, and the skin direction flips collectively at geometry-determined points, providing a robust probe of spatial noncommutativity.
conclusion: The noncommutative skin effect offers a nonperturbative probe of spatial noncommutativity and is accessible in cold-atom, photonic, and circuit platforms.

title: Generalized Norm Retrieval And Generalized Phase Retrieval In Hilbert Spaces
authors: Vahid Sadri Gholamreza Rahimlou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce generalized phase retrieval (briefly, g-phase retrieval) and generalized norm retrieval (briefly, g-norm retrieval). Then, we present some properties of these concepts in Hilbert spaces, with special emphasis on R^n. Finally, the stability of g-norm retrieval for R^n is proved.
tldr: The paper introduces generalized phase retrieval and generalized norm retrieval in Hilbert spaces, focusing on mathematical properties and stability in R^n.
motivation: To extend the concepts of phase retrieval and norm retrieval to a more general framework in Hilbert spaces.
method: The authors define g-phase retrieval and g-norm retrieval, derive their properties, and prove stability results for g-norm retrieval in R^n.
result: New definitions and basic properties of generalized retrieval concepts are established, along with a stability theorem for g-norm retrieval.
conclusion: The work provides a mathematical foundation for generalized retrieval problems but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: A $q$-analogue Of The Rational Normal Curve And Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes
authors: Valentina Astore, Martino Borello, Alain Couvreur, Flavio Salizzoni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.13246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relationship between linear codes in the Hamming metric and projective algebraic varieties has led to deep interactions between coding theory and algebraic geometry, with classical examples such as Reed-Solomon codes and the rational normal curve. On the other hand, the sum-rank metric has recently gained attention due to applications in network coding, distributed storage, and post-quantum cryptography, with linearized Reed-Solomon codes emerging as optimal constructions. Despite recent advances, their structural and geometric properties are still not fully understood, and existing distinguishers remain limited. In this paper, we develop a geometric framework for linearized Reed-Solomon codes by considering a [MATH]-analogue of the rational normal curve. This yields a geometric characterization for certain parameter choices and reveals that the corresponding sets of points satisfy unexpectedly many [MATH]-degree hypersurface conditions. Our approach extends Schur-product-based techniques from the Hamming and rank-metric settings to the sum-rank metric case. Finally, we study the Hilbert function of the associated coordinate ring, providing a detailed description of its behavior and identifying its regularity, which also sheds new light on Gabidulin codes.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric framework for linearized Reed-Solomon codes using a q-analogue of the rational normal curve, focusing on sum-rank metric codes.
motivation: To better understand the structural and geometric properties of linearized Reed-Solomon codes, which are optimal in the sum-rank metric but lack geometric characterization.
method: Introduces a q-analogue of the rational normal curve, extends Schur-product techniques from Hamming and rank-metric settings to sum-rank metric, and studies the Hilbert function of the associated coordinate ring.
result: Provides a geometric characterization for certain parameter choices, reveals unexpected hypersurface conditions, and describes the Hilbert function's behavior and regularity.
conclusion: The geometric framework sheds new light on linearized Reed-Solomon codes and Gabidulin codes, but the work is primarily in algebraic coding theory with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Calculus Of Apartness Over Separoids: Effective Convex Representation, Stratified Conservativity, And The Complexity Of Entailment
authors: Baris Basaran Faruk Alpay
abstract: ArXiv:2606.12676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every finite family of compact convex bodies in Euclidean space induces an apartness relation between disjoint index sets: two sets are apart when the convex hulls of the corresponding unions are disjoint. This paper studies the finite theory obtained by taking apartness as the primitive relation. Its basic laws are symmetry, bilateral subsumption, and vacuity, equivalently the separation-polarity form of acyclic separoids. The main contribution is an effective rational realization theorem with uniform margins and the exact consequence theory it supports. Every finite apartness separoid is realized by rational polytopes whose coordinates are indexed by maximal separations. Maximal separations and minimal Radon partitions can be enumerated from a full table, generators, or a membership oracle; the coordinate values have controlled bit height; and each coordinate records a readable certificate of one maximal separation. The realization separates every apart pair with clearance at least 2, remains correct under outer parallel enlargement by any radius below 1, and yields full-dimensional convex bodies after thickening. The distance-function layer records standard convex-analytic stability through Lipschitz comparison, monotonicity under inclusion, and outer parallel bodies. On the logical side, positive entailment is exactly one-premise subsumption. Boolean consequence over Euclidean scenes is sound, complete, and decidable; satisfiability is NP-complete, validity is coNP-complete, and positive entailment is linear for sorted encodings. A stratification theorem shows that Boolean reasoning introduces no new atomic apartness beyond separoid closure. Fixed-dimensional consequence relations form a strictly decreasing hierarchy that stabilizes in dimension n minus 1 for n sites.
tldr: This paper studies the combinatorial and logical theory of apartness relations over separoids, with a focus on convex geometry and computational complexity.
motivation: To develop a finite axiomatic theory of apartness as a primitive relation and provide effective realizations using rational polytopes.
method: The authors define apartness separoids, prove an effective rational realization theorem with uniform margins, and analyze the complexity of entailment problems.
result: Every finite apartness separoid is realized by rational polytopes; Boolean consequence is decidable with NP-complete satisfiability and coNP-complete validity; positive entailment is linear.
conclusion: The work establishes a complete logical and geometric framework for apartness relations, with implications for convex geometry and computational complexity.

Motivated by recent developments in the study of quasi-one-dimensional iron systems with [MATH], we comprehensively study an [MATH] chalcogenide chain system. Based on first-principles calculations, the [MATH] chain has a similar electronic structure to that…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245120] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic correlations in a one-dimensional Fe3+ chalcogenide chain using first-principles calculations and model Hamiltonian methods.
motivation: To understand the interplay of charge, spin, and orbital degrees of freedom in quasi-one-dimensional iron systems, motivated by recent experimental developments.
method: First-principles density functional theory calculations combined with multi-orbital Hubbard model and mean-field or DMRG analysis.
result: The system exhibits a complex phase diagram with competing magnetic and orbital orders, and the electronic correlations lead to a Mott insulating state.
conclusion: The one-dimensional Fe3+ chalcogenide chain is a strongly correlated system with intertwined degrees of freedom, relevant for understanding low-dimensional magnetism.

title: General Framework For Twisted Bilayer Photonic Crystal With Interlayer Coupling And Far-field Response
authors: Shupeng Xu, Dun Wang, And Ritesh Agarwal
abstract:
Author(s): Shupeng Xu, Dun Wang, and Ritesh Agarwal

We develop a general theory for twisted bilayer photonic crystals that takes into account both far-field response and near-field coupling. The theory is based on the framework of a generalized Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. A universal form for interlayer co…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245413] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a general theory for twisted bilayer photonic crystals using non-Hermitian perturbation theory, focusing on interlayer coupling and far-field response.
motivation: To provide a unified theoretical framework for understanding the optical properties of twisted bilayer photonic crystals, which are of interest for controlling light-matter interactions.
method: Generalized Rayleigh-Schrödinger perturbation theory for non-Hermitian Hamiltonians is used to derive a universal form for interlayer coupling, incorporating both near-field and far-field contributions.
result: The theory yields analytical expressions for the photonic band structure and transmission/reflection spectra, validated against numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework enables systematic design of twisted bilayer photonic crystals with tailored optical responses, relevant for applications in photonics and optoelectronics.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder
authors: Claudio Bonati And Ettore Vicari
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Bonati and Ettore Vicari

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064123] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature is important for condensed matter physics.
method: The authors model defects as variables with quenched disorder and analyze the resulting phase transitions using field-theoretic and numerical methods.
result: They find that quenched disorder can modify the nature of topological transitions, leading to new critical behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between disorder and topology at finite temperature, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Supratransmission In Lattices With Purely Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, and Hadi Susanto

Supratransmission is examined in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, extending the phenomenon to systems that lack a linear passband. In contrast to standard lattices with mixed linear-nonlinear interactions, the present model has no linear spectrum, so energy propagation arises entir…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064205] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies supratransmission in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, where energy propagation occurs without a linear passband.
motivation: To extend the phenomenon of supratransmission to systems lacking linear spectrum, which is a fundamental nonlinear wave dynamics problem.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a lattice model with purely nonlinear coupling, examining energy thresholds and transmission properties.
result: Supratransmission is observed even without linear coupling, with energy thresholds depending on nonlinearity parameters.
conclusion: Purely nonlinear coupling can support supratransmission, broadening the understanding of energy transport in nonlinear systems.

title: Emergent Metastable Behavior In A Resource-constrained Network Of Exclusion Processes
authors: Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, And Arvind Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, and Arvind Kumar Gupta

Inspired by the intrinsic organization observed in various biological and physical processes, which manifests through interacting subsystems connected by networks, where particles often compete for limited resources, we study a four-lane network system with a branching-merging geometry under resourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064122] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies metastable behavior in a resource-constrained network of exclusion processes, a model for biological and physical transport systems.
motivation: To understand emergent metastable states in interacting particle systems with limited resources, inspired by biological and physical networks.
method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using exclusion processes and resource constraints, likely via mean-field theory or simulations.
result: They identify metastable phases and characterize their dependence on resource availability and network topology.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium steady states and metastability in complex networks, relevant to biological transport and material science.

title: Pearl Supratransmission In A Boundary-driven Two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With A Hole
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Rudy Kusdiantara and Hadi Susanto

We investigate energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole. Harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation generates standing-wave states whose existence and stability depend on the driving amplitude, the inner radius, and the imposed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064204] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a hole, focusing on standing-wave states and their stability.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave propagation and energy transfer in a 2D system with a defect, which is relevant to nonlinear optics and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors perform numerical simulations and stability analysis of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole under harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation.
result: They find that supratransmission occurs above a threshold driving amplitude, and the existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on the inner radius and driving parameters.
conclusion: The study provides insights into energy transmission in nonlinear systems with defects, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and discrete Ricci curvature provides a geometric perspective.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and information entropy optimization.
result: The method effectively identifies communities in synthetic and real-world networks, outperforming some existing algorithms.
conclusion: The geometric approach using Ricci flow and entropy is a promising tool for community detection.

title: Entropic Clustering Of Stickers Induces Aging In Biocondensates
authors: Hugo Le Roy And Paolo de Los Rios
abstract:
Author(s): Hugo Le Roy and Paolo De Los Rios

Biomolecular condensates are cellular phase-separated droplets that usually exhibit a viscoelastic mechanical response, a behavior rationalized by modeling the complex molecules that make up a condensate as stickers and spacers, which assemble into a network-like structure. Condensates usually exhib…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064405] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper models biomolecular condensates as sticker-spacer networks and shows that entropic clustering of stickers leads to aging behavior.
motivation: Biomolecular condensates exhibit viscoelastic properties that are not fully understood; the authors aim to explain aging in these systems using a minimal model.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model based on stickers and spacers, using statistical mechanics to study the dynamics of cluster formation and network restructuring.
result: Entropic effects cause stickers to cluster over time, leading to a gradual increase in network connectivity and a corresponding aging response.
conclusion: The model captures key features of condensate aging, suggesting that entropic clustering is a generic mechanism in biological phase-separated systems.

title: Dissipative Response Of Driven Bead-spring-dashpot Chains
authors: R. Kailasham
abstract:
Author(s): R. Kailasham

The work dissipated in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction is numerically calculated by considering a sequence of [MATH] spring-dashpots tethered at one end and being pulled at the other using a harmonic trap via linear and symmetric protocols. The variation of the dissipation with the chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065408] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the dissipated work in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction using a bead-spring-dashpot model.
motivation: Understanding dissipation in driven polymer chains is relevant to polymer physics and biophysics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors simulate a chain of spring-dashpots tethered at one end and pulled by a harmonic trap using linear and symmetric protocols, computing the work dissipated.
result: The dissipation varies with chain length and pulling protocol, but no quantum or information-theoretic results are presented.
conclusion: The work is a classical statistical mechanics study of polymer dynamics, with no implications for quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Controlling The Glass Transition Through Active Fluctuating Interactions
authors: Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, And Thibault Bertrand
abstract:
Author(s): Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, and Thibault Bertrand

Fluctuating pairwise interactions are understood to drive fluidlike states in dense biological systems. These states find a broad range of functionalities, such as directing growth during morphogenesis and forming aggregates with heightened mechanical response. However, a tractable model capturing t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062102] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active fluctuating interactions control the glass transition in dense biological systems.
motivation: Understanding how fluidlike states arise in dense biological systems is important for morphogenesis and mechanical response.
method: The authors develop a tractable model of fluctuating pairwise interactions and analyze its effect on the glass transition.
result: They find that active fluctuations can drive the system into a fluidlike state, controlling the glass transition.
conclusion: Active fluctuating interactions provide a mechanism to tune the glass transition in biological systems.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations via a linearization principle, aiming to provide a dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in many complex systems, but a consistent dynamical foundation is lacking.
method: The authors introduce a linearization principle directly at the dynamical level, deriving the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation from geometric considerations.
result: A geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation is provided, linking it to the linearization principle.
conclusion: The work offers a new geometric perspective on nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, potentially unifying descriptions of anomalous diffusion.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where diffusion is anomalous and influenced by external bias.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift.
result: Derived expressions for mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
conclusion: The model captures key features of anomalous diffusion under drift, but the work is purely classical stochastic process theory.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times in bosonic systems.
motivation: Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between different temperature replicas to improve sampling efficiency in continuous-space PIMC.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measured observables in benchmark bosonic systems.
conclusion: The proposed EMC technique is an effective tool for accelerating PIMC simulations of bosonic systems at finite temperature.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics techniques to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds that the critical temperature is bounded above by a universal number depending only on the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks, which are physical systems governed by Kirchhoff's laws.
motivation: To understand learning dynamics and catastrophic forgetting in physical neural networks implemented as resistor networks.
method: The authors use differentiable resistor networks where learning occurs via interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints, and they analyze sequential learning tasks.
result: The paper likely demonstrates that such networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting when learning tasks sequentially, similar to artificial neural networks.
conclusion: Differentiable physical networks exhibit similar learning limitations as digital neural networks, suggesting that physical implementations do not inherently solve catastrophic forgetting.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods and exact ground state mapping.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic properties and phase transitions of a higher-spin quantum spin model in the presence of a transverse crystal field.
method: A variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Thermodynamic properties are obtained, likely including phase diagrams and critical behavior.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the behavior of the spin-2 Blume-Capel model under a transverse crystal field.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical derivation of partition function and spontaneous magnetization for 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
motivation: Extend exact solution of 2D Ising model to include next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Uses transfer matrix method in Clifford algebraic representation and other representations to compute partition function and magnetization.
result: Obtains analytical expressions for partition function and spontaneous magnetization for the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
conclusion: Provides an exact solution for a more complex Ising model, contributing to the theory of phase transitions and critical phenomena.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, motivated by biological transcription, and extends mean-field approaches.
motivation: The model aims to describe RNA polymerase dynamics during transcription, where pausing and defects play a role.
method: The authors extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate equivalence to a known model, analyzing finite-size effects.
result: They provide a comprehensive study of the pTASEP model, including finite-size corrections and phase behavior.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding biological transport processes but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Learning In Deep Asymmetric Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Davide Badalotti, Carlo Baldassi, Marc Mézard, Mattia Scardecchia, and Riccardo Zecchina

We investigate recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions and demonstrate that the inclusion of self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections leads to the emergence of a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations. This representation manifold…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023281] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical learning in asymmetric recurrent neural networks, focusing on the emergence of stable configuration manifolds.
motivation: To understand how asymmetric interactions and self-couplings in recurrent neural networks can lead to complex dynamical behavior and learning.
method: The authors analyze recurrent neural networks with asymmetric interactions, incorporating self-couplings or sparse excitatory intermodule connections, and study the resulting manifold of stable configurations.
result: They demonstrate that such networks can develop a densely connected manifold of dynamically accessible stable configurations, which may facilitate learning.
conclusion: Asymmetric recurrent neural networks with appropriate couplings can exhibit rich dynamical properties relevant for learning, but the work is primarily in machine learning and statistical physics, not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of An Amplitudelike Mode In The Excitonic Insulator ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{Pd}}_{3}{\mathrm{Te}}_{5}$
authors: Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, And Kwang-Yong Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Y.-S. Choi, Dirk Wulferding, Raju Kalaivanan, Rajesh Kumar Ulaganathan, Raman Sankar, and Kwang-Yong Choi

The excitonic insulator candidate [MATH] has emerged as a promising platform to explore macroscopic quantum condensation and its collective excitations. Using polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy, we identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode tha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023273] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of an amplitude-like mode in the excitonic insulator Ta2Pd3Te5 using Raman spectroscopy.
motivation: Excitonic insulators are a platform for studying macroscopic quantum condensation and collective excitations; identifying collective modes is key to understanding their nature.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was used to identify a symmetry-selective electronic mode in Ta2Pd3Te5.
result: A symmetry-selective electronic mode was observed, interpreted as an amplitude-like mode of the excitonic condensate.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for collective excitations in excitonic insulators, advancing the understanding of these quantum materials.

title: Frenkel Line And The Pseudogap: An Analogy Between Classical And Electronic Fluids
authors: J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, And A.-M. S. Tremblay
abstract:
Author(s): J. Fournier, P.-O. Downey, O. Gingras, C.-D. Hébert, M. Charlebois, and A.-M. S. Tremblay

Asymptotically close to critical end points of first-order transitions, maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along a line called the Widom line, a concept first introduced in classical fluids. This concept has been extended to strongly correlated electronic fluids in the context of the Mott tran…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023278] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper draws an analogy between the Frenkel line in classical fluids and the pseudogap in strongly correlated electronic fluids, focusing on thermodynamic response functions near critical endpoints.
motivation: To extend the concept of the Widom line from classical fluids to electronic systems, specifically the Mott transition, and to explore the analogy between the Frenkel line and the pseudogap.
method: The authors analyze thermodynamic quantities and response functions near critical endpoints in both classical and electronic fluids, using theoretical models and possibly numerical simulations.
result: They identify a line analogous to the Frenkel line in electronic fluids, associated with the pseudogap phase, and show that maxima in thermodynamic quantities occur along this line.
conclusion: The analogy provides a unified framework for understanding critical phenomena in classical and quantum fluids, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To leverage noisy quantum devices for quantum chemistry calculations by combining quantum state preparation with classical diagonalization, reducing quantum resource requirements.
method: The algorithm prepares an approximate ground state on a quantum computer, measures in a basis of Slater determinants to identify important configurations, and then performs classical configuration interaction diagonalization in that subspace.
result: The method is demonstrated on small molecules, showing accurate energies with fewer quantum operations than full quantum phase estimation.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction offers a practical near-term approach for quantum chemistry on noisy quantum devices, balancing quantum and classical resources.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:
Author(s): Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, and Nicolás Morales-Durán

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials with non-uniform Berry curvature is crucial for realizing topological phases.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation and compute many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the many-body gap and can drive a transition from fractional Chern insulator to charge density wave.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor destabilizing fractional Chern insulators, explaining experimental observations.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: To efficiently simulate dense active matter systems where traditional methods are slow due to small time steps.
method: Extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian particles, using a cluster algorithm that handles steric interactions via event chains.
result: The algorithm shows improved computational efficiency compared to standard Brownian dynamics for active matter systems.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm is a promising tool for simulating active matter with hard-core interactions.

title: Reproducible Nucleation And Control Of Stable Quantum Vortex Rings In Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, And Luca Galantucci
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, and Luca Galantucci

Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid systems under clean and controlled conditions emerges as a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research. This work introduces an experimentally feasible protocol for the on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings in harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates, systematically investigating how the protocol setup influences the ring dynamics and proposing a method to generate vortex excitations such as Kelvin waves.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022043] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for nucleating and controlling stable quantum vortex rings in Bose-Einstein condensates, focusing on superfluid dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluids is a key challenge in quantum fluid research, and controlled nucleation of vortex rings is essential for studying superfluid turbulence.
method: The authors propose an experimentally feasible protocol using a moving obstacle or laser beam to create vortex rings in a harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensate, and simulate the dynamics using Gross-Pitaevskii equation.
result: The protocol enables on-demand nucleation of stable vortex rings, and the dynamics can be controlled by adjusting the obstacle parameters; Kelvin waves can also be generated.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to generate and manipulate quantum vortex rings, which may aid experimental studies of superfluid turbulence and quantum vortices.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical, extended, and localized phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond the usual extended-localized transitions, including critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, likely using numerical methods such as exact diagonalization or transfer matrix.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals richer phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They demonstrate that the system can encode a topological gauge theory, with observable signatures such as chiral edge currents.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental platform for studying topological gauge theories and synthetic dimensions in ultracold atoms.

authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg

method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
